## 4. The semantic layer (WP3): build + check file

**Steps** (`refreshLeanFacts`, see `packages/runner/src/semantic/types.ts`):
1. **Memory guard.** `readMemAvailable()` ≥ `minAvailableBytes` (default 2 GiB), else return status `low-memory` without spawning. The board shows "Lean paused: low memory (x GB available)"; the next save or the Refresh button retries.
2. **Toolchain and project.** `lean-toolchain` (trimmed) must read `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`, else `unsupported-toolchain` (syntactic mode banner, D-7). `lake-manifest.json` must exist (the sandbox keeps the root read-only, so Lake could not write one) and its `packages` must be empty, else `unsupported-project` with a detail ("lake-manifest.json is missing" / "this project has Lake dependencies (…): M1 checks only dependency-free models; Mathlib needs an explicit opt-in, M4"). Nothing is spawned in either case.
3. **Build in place.** Hash every module source (sha256) first and keep the texts (column conversion needs them). `runLean({ shadowDir: root, argv: [<toolchain>/bin/lake, 'build'], maskPaths: [root/.git if it exists], memoryMax, timeoutMs, runId, signal })`.
4. **Parse Lake's log** (stdout and stderr). Line shapes verified on Lake 5.0 / Lean 4.35 (review probe, 2026-11-01):
   - progress: `✔ [i/n] Built <Module> (…)`; `⚠ [i/n] Replayed <Module>` (Lake replays the stored messages of up-to-date modules, so warnings such as "declaration uses `sorry`" appear on every build); `✖ [i/n] Building <Module> (…)` (failed);
   - `trace: …` lines (ignored);
   - messages: `error|warning|info: <path>:<line>:<col>: <first line>`, then every following line up to the next recognised line is a continuation (Hint/Note paragraphs, indented terms) and belongs to the message text;
   - `Some required targets logged failures:` followed by `- <Module>` lines; `error: build failed`; `Build completed successfully (n jobs).`
   Lean lines are 1-based and columns are 0-based code points: convert to 0-based lines and UTF-16 characters using the source text of step 3. Lake gives no end position: ranges are zero-width.
5. **Module states.** Modules = `<library>.lean` and `<library>/**.lean`. Imports come from each file's header (`import X` lines). `failed` = Lake said so (Lake then *deletes* that module's `.olean`/`.ilean`: verified twice); `dependency-failed` = a project import is failed or dependency-failed; `not-built` = not in the root's import closure; otherwise `fresh` (built now or up to date). Failed, dependency-failed and not-built modules are never imported by the check file, even when old `.olean` files exist for them.
6. **Read `.ilean`** for fresh modules: `.lake/build/lib/lean/<Module/Path>.ilean`, JSON, `version` 5 (anything else: no decls for that module, status `check-errors` with a detail). Verified shape on Lean 4.35 (Spyro, 2026-11-01):
   ```json
   { "version": 5, "module": "Model.Spyro.Main", "directImports": [["Model.Spyro.Vocabulary", false, false, false]],
     "decls": { "Spyro.cynder_dark_past": [23, 0, 24, 52, 24, 7, 24, 23], … },
     "references": { "{\"c\":{\"m\":\"Model.Spyro.Vocabulary\",\"n\":\"Spyro.HasDarkPast\"}}":
                       { "definition": null, "usages": [[24, 34, 24, 45, "Spyro.cynder_dark_past"]] }, … } }
   ```
   `decls[name]` = full range (from the docstring) then selection range, 0-based; columns are UTF-16 (verified with non-BMP characters on the line). Each usage = range + the *parent declaration* that contains it → `DeclFacts.refs`. A `definition` array has 4 elements, or 5 when Lean records a parent. Names starting with `_private.` are skipped. A reference whose `definition` parent is another declaration (structure fields: `Spyro.Rec.past` → `Spyro.Rec`) gives `DeclFacts.parent`. Lean also records elaborated projections (`d0.holds.2` gives a ref to `And.right` on the `2`).
7. **Check file** on stdin to `lake env lean --stdin --json` under runLean, importing every fresh module:
   ```lean
   import Model.Spyro.Vocabulary
   import Model.Spyro.Main
   set_option pp.fullNames true
   set_option pp.proofs false
   #check @Spyro.cynder_dark_past        -- "Spyro.cynder_dark_past : Prop"
   #print Spyro.cynder_dark_past         -- "@[reducible] def Spyro.cynder_dark_past : Prop :=\nSpyro.HasDarkPast Spyro.cynder"
   #print axioms Spyro.cynder_dark_past  -- "'Spyro.cynder_dark_past' depends on axioms: [Classical.choice,\n Spyro.Character, …]"
   #check type_of% @Spyro.HasDarkPast    -- axioms and opaques only: "Spyro.Character → Prop : Type"
   …
   ```
   Names are written with M0's `formatDeclName`. Messages are attributed by their 1-based `pos.line` (M0 `footprintsFromMessages` pattern). Parsing (outputs verified by the review's probe):
   - `#check`: `type` = text after the first ` : `, whitespace normalised (long types wrap onto indented lines: `Spyro.d3.holds : Spyro.a_long_name →\n  Spyro.b_long_name → Spyro.cynder_not_good → Spyro.d3`).
   - `#print`: the keyword before the name (`axiom`, `theorem`, `def`, `opaque`, `structure`, `inductive`, `class`), the `@[…]` attributes, and for `def`s the value after `:=` (`value`; theorems print `:=\n⋯` under `pp.proofs false`). **`instance` is not visible there**: a Prop-valued instance prints as a theorem (`theorem Spyro.instNonemptyCharacter : Nonempty Spyro.Character :=\nSpyro.Character.exists`), a data instance as `@[instance_reducible] def …`. So `kind: 'instance'` is set when the declaration's source text (after docstring, attributes and modifiers) starts with the `instance` keyword.
   - `#print axioms`: the list (M0 `parseAxiomsMessage`; it spans lines), `usesSorry` = contains `sorryAx`.
   - `#check type_of% @N` (axioms and opaques; others optional): `typeSort` = text after the last ` : ` (`Prop`: N proves a proposition, so an axiom of sort Prop is an assertion; `Type`: a data, function or predicate symbol; `Type 1`: a sort such as `axiom T : Type`).
   - An error message on a line → `error`.
   Measured: check ~0.3 s and ~480 MB RSS; build ~1.2 s and ~500 MB RSS for Spyro (unsandboxed probe).
8. **Re-hash** the sources; any module whose hash changed during the refresh becomes `stale`.
9. **Docstrings**: the text between `/--` and `-/` at the start of each declaration's full range.

**Mapping to the board's `SemanticSummary`** (WP4): `ok` → `fresh` (or `stale` when files changed since); `build-errors`/`check-errors` → `failed` with `errorCount` (facts for fresh modules are still used); `low-memory` → `paused-low-memory`; `unsupported-toolchain` → same; `unsupported-project` → `disabled` with the detail (+ diagnostic TL201); `could-not-start` → `disabled` with detail ("sandbox unavailable: …"); `timeout`/`oom`/`cancelled` → `failed` with detail. Previous facts stay in use after a failed refresh (marked stale where hashes differ).

**Why not `collectAxioms` or a compiled extractor in M1?** 03 §5 keeps M1 tool-free; `#print axioms` gives the same list and the `.ilean` index gives exact references without running any code beyond Lean itself. The compiled extractor (closure hashes for G5) arrives in M2.

## 6. Core semantics (WP1, WP2)

### 6.1 Binding, command starts, ids and the D-2(b) convention
- A block binds by `lean:` (pinned; the first name is the statement) or else by adjacency (the next declaration with no blank line in between; docstring, `@[…]`, modifiers and plain comments may intervene; another block, a blank line or EOF = code-less; TL013 when a declaration follows after a blank line). Names resolve against the enclosing namespaces (`_root_.` honoured). Pinned names are fully qualified as telelean writes them (D-8); WP2 falls back to resolving a pinned name against the block's enclosing namespaces when no declaration has the exact name.
- **Command starts** (where a declaration's span ends; WP1): a line at column 0 that begins with a declaration keyword (`axiom theorem lemma def abbrev opaque instance example inductive coinductive structure class mutual`), a modifier (`private public protected noncomputable unsafe partial nonrec scoped local meta`), `@[`, `/--`, `/-!`, `/-`, a `--` line comment, `end`, `namespace`, `section`, `open`, `export`, `variable`, `universe`, `set_option`, `attribute`, `notation`/`infix`/`infixl`/`infixr`/`prefix`/`postfix`, `macro`, `macro_rules`, `syntax`, `elab`, `deriving`, `initialize`, a `#…` command, `import`; or EOF.
- **Ids.** A block without `id:` gets `deriveId(natural_name)`, unique within its file (WP1, TL112 info). WP2 resolves a derived id that collides with any other id in the workspace by suffixing (`-2`, `-3`, …; files in path order); TL006 is reported only for duplicated *written* ids.
- **D-2(b).** The statement must be a Prop-valued `abbrev`/`def` (`abbrev n : Prop := S`); its justification is the declaration named `n.holds` (anywhere in the project; by convention right after the statement). Anything else bound to a block (a bare axiom or theorem) is flagged TL113 ("write `abbrev n : Prop := …` and `axiom n.holds : n`") and the node is `ill-formed` (M1 is strict: telelean writes and reads only the approved D-2(b) form).
- **Pinning (D-8).** Whenever telelean edits a block whose node is formalised by adjacency, the same plan also writes `lean: <fully-qualified statement>` (like the derived-id write-back), so later inserted declarations cannot rebind it.
- Code shown on a card = the source text from the statement's start (docstring included) to the end of `n.holds`, when contiguous (only blank lines/comments between); otherwise the pieces joined by a blank line (refs are mapped per piece). `codeLoc` = where it starts.

### 6.2 D-11 kind changes as implementable logic
`kindChangeImpact` (done, graph only, for drop zones) and `planKindChange` (WP2, with facts) share this table. Let S = statement, H = `S.holds`, hk = H's kind (`absent`/`axiom`/`theorem`; `other` is treated as `theorem`), deps = declarations using H (transitively, from `DeclFacts.refs`).

| from→to | code-less | hk = absent | hk = axiom | hk = theorem |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G→D | type only | type only ("counts as derived once proved") | type only → pending promotion | type only ("already proved") |
| G→A | type only | type + `add-holds-axiom` (+ optional rationale) | type only | type + `holds-theorem-to-axiom` (archived) |
| D→A | type only | type + `add-holds-axiom` | type only | type + `holds-theorem-to-axiom` (archived) |
| A→D | type only | type only | type only → **pending promotion** (axiom stays, flag `claimed`; dependents `rests-on-claimed`) | type only |
| A→G, D→G | type only | type only | deps = ∅: type + `remove-holds`; deps ≠ ∅: needs `dependents` | same, with `archive: true` |

With deps ≠ ∅ and no `dependents` choice → `ActionError('needs-confirmation', …, deps)` (deps = node ids, plus fully-qualified names of untracked declarations). `mark-broken` → `remove-holds` (dependents stop compiling and show as not checked/ill-formed after the refresh). **`rewrite`** → requires every touched file to be fresh (else `facts-stale`). Let C = the declarations using H (a declaration d uses x when one of d's `DeclFacts.refs` names x), closed under "uses a member of C". Refuse with `unsafe` (listing them) when C contains a non-theorem (a def/abbrev/instance/opaque cannot take a hypothesis without changing its type), or, when H is an axiom, when a declaration whose `axioms` list H is neither in C nor H itself (a use the references do not show, e.g. through notation). Otherwise: hypName = `h_<last component of S>` (suffixed `_2`, `_3`, … until it occurs as a token in none of C's declarations); for each d ∈ C: `add-hypothesis(d, hypName, hypType = S relative to d's namespace, replace = d's refs to H)` — the binder goes **right after d's name, before its existing binders**, so that `(c h)` is a correct partial application for callers that pass further arguments — and, for each c ∈ C referenced in d, `apply-hypothesis(d, hypName, replace = d's refs to c)`; then `remove-holds`. Each d becomes `theorem d (h : S) … : …`, i.e. conditional on the node (D-2(b)). Spans come from `DeclFacts.refs` converted to offsets of the current text (valid because the files are fresh). The board card moves to `to` at `beforeId` (layout change in the same plan). Pending promotion needs no markup: it is derived (a DERIVATION whose H is an axiom); writing the proof by hand (replacing `axiom` with `theorem … := …`) makes it `proved` on the next refresh.

**Other plans** (WP2): `add-node` id = `deriveId(naturalName, taken)` over every id in the workspace (written and derived); `preferredId` is ignored in M1 (the webview's optimistic card is replaced when the graph arrives; `ActionOutcome.nodeId` tells it the final id). The sentence is written verbatim (trimmed only).

**History and toast labels** (one line, the sentence cut to 60 characters with `…`): `Add assumption: <sentence>` (derivation/goal likewise); `Edit sentence: <new sentence>`; `Edit why: <sentence>`; `Set stance: <stance> (<sentence>)`; `Set source: <source> (<sentence>)`; `Delete: <sentence>`; `Make Goal: <sentence>` (+ ` (dependents rewritten)` / ` (dependents marked broken)`); `Move: <sentence>`; `These suffice: <target sentence> ← <n> premises`; `New subject: <S>`; `Undo: <label>`; `Redo: <label>`; `Revert to: <label> (<time>)`; `Manual edits`; `Initial state`; `Initialize model`.

### 6.3 Status derivation (D-15) and edges (D-13)
`formal`: `informal` (code-less) · `formalized` (the statement is a Prop abbrev/def: in the facts, or syntactically when the file has no usable facts) · `ill-formed` (TL101 statement not found, TL113 not a Prop abbrev/def, or a Lean error inside the node's statement or `.holds` declaration).

**Which facts.** A fresh file (hash = facts) uses its facts. A **stale** file (hash differs) keeps a declaration's previous facts **by name** while its current syntactic keyword agrees with the facts' kind (flag `stale`; `refs` dropped; `uses`, `presupposes`, `axioms` kept), so statuses do not flicker while the user types. Otherwise, and for files in failed / dependency-failed / not-built modules or with no facts at all, only the syntactic keyword counts: an `axiom` H counts as an axiom; a `theorem` H counts as **not proved** (proof `none`) with `not-checked` (plus `stale` in a stale file). The board never shows "proved" without Lean.

`proof` (per node, from H as determined above):

| type | H absent | H axiom | H theorem, no `sorryAx` | H theorem with `sorryAx` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ASSUMPTION | none + `missing-holds` (TL117) | assumed | proved/conditional + `provable-assumption` (TL106) | none + `uses-sorry` |
| DERIVATION | none | pending-promotion + `claimed` | proved / conditional | none + `uses-sorry` (TL115) |
| GOAL | none | assumed + TL116 ("make it an Assumption?") | proved / conditional + `proved-goal` (TL105) | none + `uses-sorry` |

- **Proved vs conditional**: normalise H's `#check` type (every whitespace run → one space). Equal to S → `proved { footprint }`. Otherwise split at top-level ` → ` (outside brackets; not when the type starts with `∀`, `∃` or `fun`): the last part is S and every other part is exactly some node's statement name → `conditional { on: those nodes, footprint }`; any other type → none + `holds-mismatch` (TL114).
- **Footprint** = H's `axioms`, mapped: a node's `n.holds` (any subject) → its id; a presupposition axiom → `presup:<name>`; standard axioms and vocabulary symbols (sorts, predicates, functions, constants) → dropped; `sorryAx` → handled above; anything else (an unmarked assertion, an `axiom c : T` constant, …) → `axiom:<name>` + TL103. Theorems never appear in `#print axioms` (verified: `theorem g2.holds : g2 := d0.holds.2` lists only d0's assumptions), so a proof through a derivation shows that derivation's assumptions: exactly D-1's "which beliefs a result rests on".
- **Flags**: `rests-on-claimed` if a footprint node is pending promotion; `self-evident` if proved with no node in the footprint; `existence-commitment` + TL108 (info) if the footprint has a presupposition that neither the node's own `presupposes` nor any footprint node's `presupposes` contains (D-3b: an existence assumption the proof needs but no statement mentions); TL102 (warning) when the proof is conditional (lists `on`) or its footprint contains a GOAL node (a goal asserted as an axiom, TL116).
- **Edges** (only edges with both ends in the subject go into its graph):
  - declared `premise` edges from `premises:`;
  - **verified edges from references, not from footprints.** direct(v) = the nodes u whose `.holds` the proof of v uses: start at v's `.holds` `DeclFacts.refs` and follow references through declarations that belong to no node (untracked lemmas, defs) until a node's `.holds` is reached. One edge u→v (`where: 'proof'`) per u ∈ direct(v), plus one edge u→v with `conditional: true` per u ∈ on(v). (A footprint-based edge set would miss every derivation→goal arrow and make `proofDependents` report "nothing uses it" for a derivation that a goal's proof uses, so D→G would delete a `.holds` that others use — exactly what D-11 forbids.) Facts for a stale file: edges by name as above; no facts: no verified edges;
  - `lean-ref` edges: v's statement refs naming another node's statement (`where: 'statement'`);
  - **mismatch flags, only when v is proved or conditional**: closure(v) = transitive closure of direct(v) ∪ on(v); rests(x) = the assumption-level nodes x stands for ({x} unless x is proved or conditional, else its footprint nodes ∪ on). `declared-unused` (TL109, hint) on the premise edge p→v when p ∉ closure(v); `used-undeclared` (TL107, warning) on the verified edge u→v when u ∉ premises(v) and rests(u) ⊄ ⋃ rests(p) over p ∈ premises(v). So a proof that routes through a derivation of the declared premises is not flagged, and an unproved goal's declared premises are never "unused".
- `not-checked` when the node's module is failed/dependency-failed/not-built or no facts exist; `stale` when its file's hash differs from the facts.
- **Lean messages** become `BoardDiagnostic`s with code `LEAN`, the file and range; `nodeId` = the node whose bound declarations contain the message start (an error there makes that node `ill-formed`).

### 6.4 Vocabulary, "uses", refs, glosses, presuppositions
- **Vocabulary items** = declarations of the subject's modules (from the facts, else syntactic `DeclInfo`s) bound to no node, except auxiliary declarations with a `parent` (structure fields: shown inside their parent's item) and the presupposition instances below. Classification (D-3 simple shape check; "sort" = a project sort):
  - `axiom T : Type` → `sort`;
  - `axiom X : Nonempty T` with T a sort → `presupposition`, attached to T (`VocabItem.presupposes` / the sort's `presupposition`);
  - `instance : Nonempty T := <T's presupposition>` (anonymous or named) → **not listed** (plumbing for the chip). Lean prints it as a theorem (`Spyro.instNonemptyCharacter`) and the syntactic `DeclInfo` of an anonymous instance has no name: match facts to syntax by the declaration's start line;
  - an axiom whose `typeSort` is `Prop` and that is no node's `.holds` → `unmarked-axiom` + TL104 (a hidden assumption);
  - an axiom or opaque of type `A₁ → … → Aₙ → Prop` → `predicate` (arity n; n = 0 allowed, `axiom P0 : Prop`); + TL111 `shape-violation` when some Aᵢ is not a sort;
  - `opaque c : T` (T a sort) → `constant`; `opaque f : A₁ → … → B` (all sorts) → `function`; the same shapes declared with `axiom` → same kind + TL111 ("declare it `noncomputable opaque` so its existence presupposition shows": an axiom constant asserts existence silently);
  - other axioms (`axiom T : Type 1`, `Sort u`, non-sort data types, …) → `other` + TL111;
  - def/abbrev/structure/inductive/class/instance → `definition`, with `definitional-choice` (VocabFlag, and the StatusFlag on the node) when it lies in some node's statement closure (D-4; M1 only flags it). A Prop-valued def/abbrev without a block is an untracked statement, also a `definition`; its `.holds` axiom is an `unmarked-axiom` (TL104), its `.holds` theorem a `lemma`;
  - theorems → `lemma`.
  Without facts (syntactic mode, files never checked) the same rules run on the declaration text (keyword, the text after the name's `:`). Display order: sort, predicate, function, constant, presupposition, definition, lemma, unmarked-axiom, other; file order within a kind.
- **Gloss** = the docstring. `glossBy: 'user'` in M1 (no agent); M2 will mark agent-worded docstrings.
- **`lean.uses`** (request #23): the statement's own refs that name vocabulary items, then — breadth-first, first-occurrence order, no duplicates — those reached through referenced node statements and referenced vocabulary definitions (the statement closure). Sorts appear only where written (e.g. `∀ (g : Game)`). A name from another subject's vocabulary (explicit import, D-10) is kept fully qualified. Never hard-coded: no facts for the statement → `uses` absent and the webview hides the line; stale → kept by name.
- **`lean.refs`** (request #25): refs of the card's declarations that name a vocabulary item or another node's statement/`.holds` (then `nodeId` is set), with the range converted to `code`-relative positions; only when the file is fresh. Other refs (core constants such as `Nat`, elaborated projections such as `And.right`) are dropped.
- **`lean.presupposes`** (tray chips, D-3b): presupposition axioms in the statement's `#print axioms` list (constants force them through `Nonempty`; verified: `cynder_dark_past` → `Character.exists`; through other nodes' abbrevs too, since `#print axioms` is transitive).
- **`VocabItem.usedBy`** = nodes whose `uses` (or `presupposes`) contain the item.

### 6.7 Escaping (D-8; verification FV-5)
A value is written raw unless it contains a comment delimiter, starts with `"`, contains a line break or control character, or has leading/trailing spaces; then it is a JSON string in which every `/` followed by `-` is written `/` (so `/-` becomes the 7 characters backslash u 0 0 2 f -) and every other `/` preceded by `-` is written `\/` (so `-/` becomes `-\/`). The Markdown body, and docstrings written by `set-docstring`, use `-\/` and `/\-` (doc comments nest too). The D-9 mirror compares a docstring with `escapeBodyText(old natural_name)`. Programmatic edits are safe from the Lean extension's `\`-input rewriting (research r4).

## 8. Undo vs history (WP4)

**Undo/Redo** (D-17): per root and subject, in memory (lost on window reload), at most 100 entries. An entry is the materialised `FileChange[]` of one action (whole-file before/after, sidecars included) plus its label. Undo of an entry: for each file, if the current text equals `after`, write `before`; otherwise apply the reverse patch (`diff` 9.0.0 `structuredPatch`/`applyPatch`, no fuzz) to the current text; a file created by the action is deleted only if unchanged; any failure refuses the whole undo (`conflict`: "<file> changed since; use History to revert"). The undo is applied like an action (snapshotted "Undo: <label>") and moves to the redo stack; a new action clears redo. Revert, undo and redo are themselves undoable.

**History** (D-33, A3): durable git snapshots, per subject.
- **Refs**: `refs/telelean/<rootKey>/subjects/<S>` (one chain per subject) and `refs/telelean/<rootKey>/project`; `rootKey` = `root` when the model root is the repository top level, else the relative path with `/`→`.`, other characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` → `_`, plus `-<8 hex of sha1(relpath)>`. Validate with `git check-ref-format`.
- **Snapshot** = a commit whose tree holds exactly the scope's files (`subjectSnapshotScope` / `projectSnapshotScope` in `paths.ts`), paths relative to the model root, parent = the chain's tip. Message: the label, a blank line, then trailers `Telelean-Action`, `Telelean-Subject`, `Telelean-Nodes`, `Telelean-Format: 1`. Author and committer `telelean <telelean@localhost>` (configurable), date = now. File contents come from the TextSource (what the user sees, unsaved typing included).
- **Plumbing only, never the user's index, branches or hooks**: `hash-object -w`, a temporary index file in a fresh temp dir (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`) or `mktree`, `write-tree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`; every call with `-c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c gc.auto=0 -c core.fsmonitor=false`, env `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and the explicit author/committer environment. No `checkout`, `add` on the real index, `reset`, `gc`, `prune`, `push`, `fetch` or `remote`.
- **When**: before applying an action, each touched scope whose current files differ from its tip gets a "Manual edits" snapshot; after applying, each touched scope gets the action's snapshot; a subject with no chain gets "Initial state" when its board opens. Layout-only changes (re-order) are not snapshotted on their own (they ride along in the next snapshot); they are still undoable.
- **Revert to entry X** (subject S): snapshot S's current state if it differs from the tip, then write X's tree over S's scope (files in X written, files in scope but not in X deleted) through the EditApplier, labelled "Revert to: <X's label> (<time>)", snapshotted, undoable. Project files are never reverted by a subject revert.
- **Preview**: `historyDiff(subject, entryId, 'parent' | 'current')` → WP5 opens VS Code's multi-file diff (`vscode.changes`) on a read-only `telelean-history:` document provider.
- **Storage counter**: per subject `git rev-list --objects --disk-usage <subject ref> --not --branches --tags --remotes`; overall the same over all of the root's `refs/telelean/<rootKey>/…` refs; "disk, not RAM". Cache for 10 s.
- **Keep last N** (`prune`): recreate the chain's last N commits with the same trees, messages and dates (oldest kept becomes a root commit), `update-ref` with old-value check. No gc: git's own housekeeping reclaims the space later (the counter drops at once because it counts reachable objects).
- **Unavailable**: no repository → `no-repo` (offer `git init`); no git → `git-missing`; setting off → `disabled`. Actions still work without history.

## 12. Risks

| # | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | `.ilean` is an internal format (v5 on 4.35) | The toolchain is pinned (D-7); unknown versions degrade to "no refs/uses" with a clear detail, never wrong data |
| R2 | In-place builds race the user's Lean server on the same `.lake` | Lake has **no** build lock (removed in lean4#2445; see `Lake/Util/Lock.lean` in the toolchain sources), so races are possible when a save makes both rebuild. Lean writes `.olean` files through a temporary file and a rename, so the usual cost is a redundant rebuild; a damaged artifact shows as an import error that the next build or a `.lake` clean fixes. One telelean refresh at a time; a failed refresh keeps the previous facts and retries on the next save; documented. A private build shadow is the fallback if this bites in practice |
| R3 | Lean message columns are code points, LSP needs UTF-16 | WP3 converts using the line text; a fixture with a non-BMP character tests it (`.ilean` columns are already UTF-16: verified) |
| R4 | Applying an edit saves the user's unsaved changes in that file | Documented (D-17 "edits are saved immediately"); the EditApplier refuses when the file changed since the plan; undo reverses only telelean's change |
| R5 | Chrome starts a native drag from text inside a draggable card | CSS cannot prevent it: Chromium's drag source search walks up from the text node to the nearest `draggable=true` ancestor, skipping children with `draggable="false"` or `-webkit-user-drag: none`. So WP6 sets the card's `draggable` attribute to `false` on `pointerdown` inside `.tl-lean` (restoring it on `pointerup`/`pointercancel`/blur) — the drag decision happens after pointerdown — and keeps `canDrag` false for such drags plus `user-select: text` on the code. AT6.16 proves it |

| R7 | Parallel stubs hide integration bugs (WP2 edit tests need WP1) | Skip gates + the integrator's end-to-end test (11.3) |

| R12 | Board graph rebuilt per keystroke | Parse cache by path+hash; debounce; research measured 27k lines in ~145 ms (Python) |

## 13. Decisions log

### 13.1 Minor decisions taken (for the user to review later)
1. **Opt-in marker** is `.telelean/config.json` (not `layout.json` as in 03 §6): config and layout are separate files.
2. **Per-subject sidecars** under `.telelean/subjects/<S>/` (layout.json, attic/; later decisions, attempts): D-12's root-level files, split by subject so a subject's history and revert stay self-contained.
3. **Per-subject history chains** (`refs/telelean/<rootKey>/subjects/<S>`) plus a project chain: revert touches only one subject; the storage counter is per subject and overall, as A3 asked.
4. **Layout-only changes are not snapshotted** on their own (still undoable); they ride along in the next snapshot.
5. **Pruning does not run `git gc`** on the user's repository; the counter drops at once, the disk space returns at git's next housekeeping.
6. **`mental_model/` is not `git init`ed by telelean's builders**: it lives inside the git-free telelean folder; the board offers "Initialize git".
7. **M1 "These suffice" declares support only** (writes `premises:`, D-13) and says that proving with Claude arrives in M2; with zero premises ("Self-evident?") it answers "available from M2".
8. **Strict D-2(b)**: a block bound to anything but a Prop abbrev/def is flagged TL113 (ill-formed) rather than guessed.
9. **New subject scaffold import order**: Vocabulary ← Inbox ← Main (Main imports Inbox), so hand-formalised Inbox nodes can be used by Main.
10. **`uses:`** = statement closure through other nodes' statements and vocabulary definitions; sorts listed only where written; inline the first 2 names then `, …`, with a `▾ N` dropdown. Clicking a node's name in the code reveals that card (an extension of the user's vocabulary-highlight idea).
11. **Glosses are shown as the user's wording in M1** (no agent yet); M2 marks agent-worded docstrings.
12. **Instances that only re-export a presupposition** are not listed as vocabulary.
13. **`wording.jsonl` and `attempts.jsonl` are not written in M1** (snapshots keep old wordings; attempts start with runs in M2).
14. **graph.json schema from zod** (`z.toJSONSchema`), because ajv is not a declared dependency and no package may be added.
15. **Runner `build` = typecheck** (`noEmit`); core is imported from source through tsconfig `paths` / vitest aliases, as the extension and webview already do.
16. **Applying an edit saves the file**, including any unsaved typing in it (D-17).
17. **Lean refresh runs in place** in the model folder (sources read-only, `.lake` writable, `.git` masked), as 03 §8.4 specifies, not in a shadow.
18. **No port-drag arrows in M1** (the tray declares support); keyboard/menu equivalents for kind changes are buttons in the expanded card.
19. **Theme colours**: contributed ids keep exactly one dot and get explicit per-theme hex defaults (no `charts.*`), plus `telelean.vocabulary` and `telelean.highlight`.
20. *(review)* **Verified arrows come from Lean's references, footprints from `#print axioms`**: a goal proved through a derivation shows the arrow from that derivation (not from the derivation's assumptions), while its footprint still lists exactly the assumptions it rests on.
21. *(review)* **Declared-vs-verified mismatches are judged at the assumption level**: a proof that routes through a derivation of the declared premises is not flagged; an unproved goal's premises are never "unused".
22. *(review)* **Stale files keep their previous facts by name** while the declaration keyword is unchanged (flag `stale`), so statuses do not flicker while typing; a theorem Lean has not checked never shows as proved.
23. *(review)* **The mechanical D-11 rewrite adds the hypothesis as the first binder** and refuses when a dependent is not a theorem or a use is invisible to Lean's references (choose "mark broken" then).
24. *(review)* **Projects with Lake dependencies (Mathlib) are refused in M1**, both by Initialize and by the refresh: D-28 asks for an explicit opt-in (M4), and building them breaks the RAM rule.
25. *(review)* **Hidden assumptions are recognised by Lean's sort check** (`#check type_of% @N` = `Prop`) rather than by guessing from the type text; an `axiom c : T` constant is flagged (TL111) because it asserts existence without a visible presupposition.
26. *(review)* **Exact scaffold texts are frozen and implemented with the contract** (`subjectScaffold`), so Initialize, New subject and the sample write identical files.
27. *(review)* **Adjacent bindings are pinned on the next telelean edit** of the block (`lean:` written, D-8), like the derived-id write-back.
28. *(review)* **The host always derives new ids itself** (`deriveId`, `n-<hex>` for non-Latin text); the webview's provisional id only matches its optimistic card.
29. *(review)* **The board gets a legend (D-15) and "Depends on / Used by" lists in the expanded card** (03 §7; also the keyboard/screen-reader route); an ASSUMPTION with declared premises shows D-13's hint "you think this follows from those — prove it?".

## 15. What the independent review changed (2026-11-01)

Evidence: a scratch copy of the Spyro fixture with extra declarations, built with the toolchain's own `lake` (`~/.elan/known-projects` unchanged), plus the toolchain's Lake sources.

1. **Verified edges and D→G dependents were wrong for derivations.** `#print axioms` lists only axioms, so `theorem g2.holds : g2 := d0.holds.2` never mentions `d0`; footprint-based edges would draw no d0→g2 arrow, and `proofDependents` would let D→G delete `d0.holds` while g2 uses it (D-11 violation). Fixed: verified edges from `.ilean` references (6.3); TL107/TL109 redefined at the assumption level.
2. **The rewrite inserted the hypothesis after existing binders**, which makes `(c h)` pass `h` to the wrong parameter whenever c has its own hypotheses. Fixed: binder first; refusals for non-theorem users and invisible uses (6.2).
3. **Instances**: Lean prints `instance : Nonempty Character := …` as a `theorem`, so "`def` + `instance_reducible` → instance" would have listed the presupposition instances as lemmas. Fixed: `instance` from the source keyword; anonymous instances matched by start line (4, 6.4).
4. **Hidden assumptions vs vocabulary** could not be told apart from type text. Added the `#check type_of% @N` probe (`typeSort`, verified to print `… : Prop` / `: Type` / `: Type 1`) and precise D-3 shape rules incl. `axiom c : T` (6.4).
5. **Long types wrap across lines** in `#check` output (verified); parsing now normalises whitespace (4, 6.3).
6. **Stale/failed files**: syntactic fallback would show a hand-edited `theorem` as proved without Lean, and flicker while typing; now previous facts by name, and unchecked theorems are never "proved" (6.3). A failed module no longer makes every node in it ill-formed: only nodes with an error in their own declarations.
7. **Mathlib/dependency projects** were not guarded at all; now refused (`unsupported-project`, Initialize `unsupported`): D-28 and the RAM rule.
8. **`planInitialize` could not know an existing `.gitignore`** (synchronous, no root): the inspection now carries it.
9. **Scaffold texts were unspecified** while WP2 and WP4 wrote them independently: exact texts frozen, `subjectScaffold` implemented and tested; built with Lean 4.35.
10. **R2 claimed "Lake's own locking"**: Lake has no build lock (removed in lean4#2445); risk text corrected.
11. **R5**: CSS/`draggable="false"` on the code cannot stop Chrome dragging the card; the attribute toggle on the card is the mechanism (12).
12. **Smaller fixes**: Lake log line shapes and replayed messages documented; command-start list for declaration spans; derived-id collisions; D-8 pinning on edit; id derivation always on the host; docstring escapes for `/-`; TL102/TL108/TL111 defined; legend, Depends on/Used by and the D-13 hint added to the board; statement-level dependents in the delete dialog; graph version seeding; git `core.fsmonitor=false` and `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` in tests; no `.telelean/config.json` outside `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/`; WP5 pretest fallback while `mental_model/` is still empty; leftover-unit checks limited to one's own run id.

239	| A→G, D→G | type only | type only | deps = ∅: type + `remove-holds`; deps ≠ ∅: needs `dependents` | same, with `archive: true` |

241	With deps ≠ ∅ and no `dependents` choice → `ActionError('needs-confirmation', …, deps)` (deps = node ids, plus fully-qualified names of untracked declarations). `mark-broken` → `remove-holds` (dependents stop compiling and show as not checked/ill-formed after the refresh). **`rewrite`** → requires every touched file to be fresh (else `facts-stale`). Let C = the declarations using H (a declaration d uses x when one of d's `DeclFacts.refs` names x), closed under "uses a member of C". Refuse with `unsafe` (listing them) when C contains a non-theorem (a def/abbrev/instance/opaque cannot take a hypothesis without changing its type), or, when H is an axiom, when a declaration whose `axioms` list H is neither in C nor H itself (a use the references do not show, e.g. through notation). Otherwise: hypName = `h_<last component of S>` (suffixed `_2`, `_3`, … until it occurs as a token in none of C's declarations); for each d ∈ C: `add-hypothesis(d, hypName, hypType = S relative to d's namespace, replace = d's refs to H)` — the binder goes **right after d's name, before its existing binders**, so that `(c h)` is a correct partial application for callers that pass further arguments — and, for each c ∈ C referenced in d, `apply-hypothesis(d, hypName, replace = d's refs to c)`; then `remove-holds`. input.summary:
I reviewed the M1 plan and its contract code and fixed what was wrong. The corrected plan is /home/zhengyew/telelean/docs/m1-plan.md (546 lines); section 15 lists each change with its evidence, section 14 logs the contract edits, and minor decisions 20-31 are mine. I checked the main claims on a scratch copy of the Spyro fixture with extra declarations, built with the toolchain's own lake; ~/.elan/known-projects stayed at 37 lines.

Problems found and fixed:
1. Verified arrows and D-11 dependents were wrong for derivations. `#print axioms` lists only axioms (verified: `theorem g2.holds := d0.holds.2` lists only d0's assumptions). So footprint-based edges would draw no derivation-to-goal arrow, and `proofDependents` would let D-to-G delete a `.holds` another proof uses, which D-11 forbids. Verified edges now come from the `.ilean` references, followed through untracked lemmas. The footprint still comes from `#print axioms`, and TL107/TL109 are judged at the assumption level.
2. The mechanical hypothesis rewrite put the new binder after the existing ones. Then `(c h)` passes `h` to the wrong parameter. The binder now goes first. The rewrite is refused (`unsafe`) when a dependent is not a theorem, or when a use doesn't show in the references.
3. Lean prints `instance : Nonempty T := T.exists` as a theorem (verified). `kind: 'instance'` now comes from the source keyword, and anonymous instances are matched by start line.
4. Hidden assumptions couldn't be told from vocabulary by type text. Added a `#check type_of% @N` probe (`DeclFacts.typeSort`, verified output) and exact D-3 shape rules, including flagging `axiom c : T` (TL111).
5. `#check` output wraps long types over several lines (verified), so the type is now whitespace-normalised before parsing.
6. Stale and failed files: the old syntactic fallback could show an unchecked theorem as proved, and statuses would flicker while typing. A stale file now keeps its previous facts by name, Lean-unchecked theorems are never shown as proved, and a build error makes only the node containing it ill-formed.
7. Projects with Lake dependencies (Mathlib) weren't guarded at all. They are now refused: new `FactsStatus` `unsupported-project`, and Initialize returns `unsupported` (D-28 explicit opt-in; the RAM rule).
8. `planInitialize` had no way to see an existing `.gitignore`. `FolderInspection` now carries its text.
9. WP2 and WP4 would have written the scaffold texts independently. The exact texts are now frozen; I implemented and tested `subjectScaffold` and built its output with Lean 4.35.
10. Core tests could not read fixture files: core has `types: []`, so no `node:fs`. Added `test/raw-imports.d.ts` for Vite `?raw` imports (verified with tsc and vitest).
11. `spyroProvedGraph()` didn't match the overlay it cites: pg-no-dark-past is pinned there, its code lacked the docstring line, and all block `loc`s were off. Corrected.
12. Risk R2 claimed Lake locks builds. It doesn't: the lock was removed in lean4#2445, as the toolchain sources show. R5 now explains that only toggling the card's `draggable` attribute lets Chrome select text in the code.

Smaller fixes:
- Lake log line formats documented, including replayed warnings and full multi-line messages.
- A list of the lines that end a declaration's span.
- Derived-id collisions resolved by suffix.
- D-8 pinning of adjacent bindings on the next edit.
- The host always derives new node ids.
- Docstring writes escape `/-` too (the plan text had lost the unicode escape characters; restored).
- TL102, TL108 and TL111 defined.
- Board: the M0 legend gains the new arrow kinds; the expanded card gets Depends on / Used by; the D-13 hint on an assumption with premises.
- The delete dialog also lists statements that mention the node.
- Graph versions seeded from `Date.now()`.
- Git calls also turn off `core.fsmonitor`; git tests set `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`.
- No `.telelean/config.json` outside `mental_model/` and `test-fixtures/`.
- A WP5 smoke-test fallback while `mental_model/` is still empty.
- Leftover-unit checks look only at your own run id.

Tests run after the fixes:
- core `npm test`: 38/38 passed;
- `tsc` clean for runner, webview (both configs) and extension;
- webview vitest 24/24, extension vitest 4/4.
- Not re-run: the runner suite (I changed only runner types and docs), Playwright and the VS Code smoke test.

Read docs/m1-plan.md first: the safety rules at the top, and sections 0 (reading fixtures with ?raw), 5.2, 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 6.7, 9, 14 and 15.

SAFETY (mandatory; also for anything you start):
- Never push, add remotes or use gh.
- Never publish or send anything to anyone.
- Network only to read docs.
- No downloads, no npm install, no new packages. Report a need in open issues.

- Write only inside your owned paths and your scratch dir /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn9/<your-label>/.
- Never touch the user's VS Code settings or extensions, ~/telelean_scripts, ~/.config, ~/.claude, ~/.elan, the npm config or the global git config.
- No sudo, no global installs. Do not run git in /home/zhengyew/telelean.
- Run free -m before heavy steps. Kill only processes you started.
- Report every effect outside the repo. Never claim a test passed unless you ran it; quote real output.

GOAL
Implement packages/core/src/markup/.
- The types are frozen in markup/types.ts. You may add OPTIONAL fields or new exports only, each recorded in plan section 14.
- Replace the stubs in markup/api.ts. You may split it into modules, as long as markup/index.ts keeps exporting every name.
- Core is pure TypeScript with no Node or DOM APIs (lib ES2023, types: []); the webview bundles it.
- Tests read fixture files through Vite ?raw imports, e.g. import mainLean from '../../../../test-fixtures/spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean?raw'. packages/core/test/raw-imports.d.ts declares them. Do not use node:fs.

REFERENCE
Port the research prototype in verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/subagent_reports/research_workflow/artifacts/r4-markup-lsp/:
- proto/telelean_ref.py (lexer, parse_block, FileModel, bind);
- proto/test_telelean_ref.py (20 tests);
- scripts/gen_lex_tests.py (the lexing cases L01-L20).
Read them as data. If you run Python at all, use python3 -I.

RULE CHANGES vs the reference (02/03)
- type: is canonical; kind: is a silent alias (no TL018).
- There is no DEFINITION kind.
- No TL016 for a missing version marker: absent means v1.
- premises is allowed on every node type (no TL012).
- Known fields (03 section 3.2):
  - id;
  - type: ASSUMPTION, DERIVATION or GOAL; lower case is accepted with a TL019 hint;
  - natural_name, rationale;
  - stance: believe, rule or supposing;
  - source: observed, reported, inferred or common;
  - asserted: YYYY-MM-DD;
  - premises, lean, supersedes, refines, tags;
  - origin: user or agent; session; worded_by: user or agent.
- Dotted keys and unknown keys are kept verbatim, in order, in extensions. An unknown non-dotted key also gets TL002.
- Required fields: type and natural_name (TL003).
- A block with no id: gets deriveId(natural_name), made unique within the file, idWritten false, and TL112 (info).
- Other diagnostics:
  - TL001 malformed line;
  - TL004 invalid value;
  - TL005 duplicate scalar field;
  - TL008 newer version (the block is kept);
  - TL009 block inside a doc or module-doc comment (ignored);
  - TL010 unterminated comment;
  - TL011 info for an ASSUMPTION without rationale;
  - TL013 hint;
  - TL014.
- Workspace-level duplicates, dangling premises, cycles and double binding belong to WP2.

LEXER (lexLean, Lean 4.35 rules)
- Double-dash line comments.
- Nested block comments.
- Doc comments (/--) and module-doc comments (/-!); the nesting scan starts right after the slash-dash.
- Strings with escapes, char literals, raw strings r#"..."#.
- Dotted identifiers with guillemet parts; isIdFirst/isIdRest include the letter-like and subscript Unicode tables of the Python.
- Numbers and single-character symbols.
- An unterminated comment runs to EOF.

PARSER (parseLeanFile; it never throws)
- A block is a plain block comment whose first non-blank line matches the @@ telelean marker with an optional vN.
- Field lines are key: value. A value starting with a double quote is a JSON string (parseFieldValue); otherwise it is the trimmed raw text. Never YAML.
- Lists split on commas, with optional brackets; a repeated list key accumulates.
- The body after --- is dedented, with its escapes kept.
- FieldLine spans let edits touch a single line.
- imports come from the header's import lines.
- Pinned lean: names are taken as written (fully qualified by convention; WP2 resolves fallbacks).

DECLARATIONS (DeclInfo), found by a header parser
- docstring, @[...] lists, modifiers (private public protected meta noncomputable unsafe partial nonrec scoped local);
- keyword, including class inductive, class abbrev, mutual and example;
- name (with guillemets), and instance (priority := ...) name;
- namespace/section/end tracking with _root_; fullName is the resolved name.
- span runs from the docstring/attribute/modifier start to the end of the last non-blank line before the next command start.
- A command start is exactly plan 6.1's list: a column-0 line beginning with a declaration keyword, a modifier, @[, a doc comment opener, a module-doc opener, a block comment opener, a double-dash line comment, end, namespace, section, open, export, variable, universe, set_option, attribute, notation/infix/infixl/infixr/prefix/postfix, macro, macro_rules, syntax, elab, deriving, initialize, a #-command or import; or EOF.
- valueStart is the first top-level :=, where or | after the signature, skipping brackets, strings and comments.

BINDING
- A pinned lean: field wins; its first name is the statement.
- Otherwise Go-style adjacency: the next declaration with no blank line between the block's closer and it. Plain comments, a docstring and attributes may sit in between.
- Another block, a blank line or EOF means code-less. Give TL013 (hint) when a declaration follows after a blank line, and TL014 for example/mutual.
- statement is fully qualified.
- Positions are UTF-16 offsets (JS string indices); ranges are LSP-style via lineIndex. CRLF files keep CRLF.

SERIALIZER
The exact rule is in plan 6.7; read the plan text for the exact characters.
- A value is raw unless it contains a comment delimiter, starts with a double quote, contains a line break or control character, or has leading/trailing spaces.
- Otherwise it is a JSON string in which:
  - every slash followed by a dash becomes the 6-character JSON unicode escape of a slash (backslash, u, 0, 0, 2, f);
  - every other slash preceded by a dash becomes backslash-slash.
- Body text uses escapeBodyText: dash-backslash-slash and slash-backslash-dash.
- renderBlock writes the opener, the v1 marker line, the fields in FIELD_ORDER, then --- and the body if any, then the closer, with no trailing newline.
- Lists are written a, b, c.

IDS (deriveId)
- NFKD, strip combining marks, lower-case; non-alphanumerics become -; at most 6 words.
- When nothing is left (non-Latin text): n- plus 6 hex digits of FNV-1a 32-bit over the UTF-8 bytes of the trimmed sentence (core has no crypto).
- Make it unique via taken with -2, -3, …
- The result must match ID_PATTERN.

TEXT PRIMITIVES
- applyTextEdits applies non-overlapping edits, in any order.
- setBlockField:
  - changes only the target line;
  - inserts a missing key at its FIELD_ORDER position;
  - removes the line for null;
  - escapes values;
  - also writes id: when idWritten is false.
- removeBlockEdits removes the comment, its line break and one blank line.
- insertBlockEdits keeps one blank line between neighbours.
  - end-of-namespace inserts before the end <ns> of the last matching namespace, else at EOF.
  - after-block inserts after the block and the declarations bound to it.

applyLeanOps
All or nothing: a non-empty problems list means nothing is applied. Semantics are in the LeanOp docs and plan 6.2.
- add-holds-axiom: insert axiom <rel>.holds : <rel> on the line after the statement declaration (rel = relativeName(statement, decl.namespace)).
- holds-theorem-to-axiom: replace the whole theorem declaration (with its docstring) by that axiom line, and return the old text in archived.
- remove-holds / remove-decl: delete the declaration with its docstring and one trailing blank line; archive it when asked.
- add-hypothesis: insert ' (<hypName> : <hypType>)' RIGHT AFTER the declaration's name, before any existing binders (the new hypothesis becomes the first explicit argument), and replace each given span by hypName.
- apply-hypothesis: wrap each span as (<occurrence> <hypName>). When the occurrence is immediately preceded by @, include the @: (@c h).
- set-docstring: replace or insert the doc comment, with the text escaped by escapeBodyText (doc comments nest, so both delimiters must be escaped).
All edits must be non-overlapping. A missing declaration or an unexpected shape goes into problems.

RUN
cd packages/core && npm test (tsc on src and test, then vitest).
Do not edit frozen files: index.ts, model.ts, facts.ts, protocol.ts, samples, the contracts/protocol/samples tests, raw-imports.d.ts.
Report the files you wrote, the real test output, any additive contract changes and the effects outside the repo.

AT1.2 The non-graph research tests (Lexing 5, Values 7, Binding 6) are ported to vitest with the 02/03 rule changes: type canonical, kind a silent alias, no DEFINITION kind, no TL016/TL018, premises allowed on any type

AT1.3 Parsing test-fixtures/spyro/Model/Spyro/Main.lean (read via ?raw) gives 4 blocks with the sample's ids, fields and block ranges (lines 4-11, 13-22, 27-36, 41-49). pg-no-dark-past is code-less; the other three are pinned to Spyro.cynder_dark_past / Spyro.new_spyro_pg / Spyro.cynder_not_good. decls include Spyro.cynder_dark_past.holds (keyword axiom, no valueStart), with spans ending on their own line. imports = [Model.Spyro.Vocabulary]. Vocabulary.lean gives 11 decls, including two anonymous instances (keyword instance, no name)

AT1.4 Escape round-trip and property test: random values over an alphabet with slash, dash, double quote, backslash, newline and space (including the two comment delimiters, slash-dash-slash, dash-slash-dash, a leading quote and leading spaces) go through renderBlock then parseLeanFile and come back identical. lexLean finds exactly one terminated block comment in every rendered block. A slash before a dash is written with the 6-character unicode escape of plan 6.7
AT1.5 renderBlock writes fields in FIELD_ORDER under the v1 marker, escapes the body, and preserves CRLF when eol is CRLF

AT1.6 setBlockField/removeBlockEdits/insertBlockEdits: only the targeted line(s) change (the rest of the file is byte-identical). A missing key is inserted at its FIELD_ORDER position; null removes the line; a derived id is written; blank-line spacing stays tidy; CRLF stays CRLF. insertBlockEdits into the subjectScaffold Inbox text (end-of-namespace) leaves exactly one blank line on each side

AT1.8 deriveId: Latin slugs of at most 6 words; uniqueness suffixes; a deterministic n-<6 hex> for non-Latin text; every result matches ID_PATTERN. Two id-less blocks with the same sentence in one file get distinct derived ids, each with TL112

AT1.9 Declaration spans follow plan 6.1's command starts: a column-0 double-dash comment, set_option, variable, open, attribute and #check lines end the preceding declaration; an indented continuation line does not; a block comment after a theorem ends it

GOAL
Implement, as pure TypeScript (no Node or DOM; the webview bundles core):
- project/index.ts: buildProjectModel, subjectGraph.
- edit/index.ts: planAction, planKindChange, planDelete.
  - subjectScaffold is ALREADY implemented with the exact texts of plan 7.1. Keep its output; contracts.test.ts guards it.
- export/graphJson.ts: toGraphJson, plus a zod schema in export/schema.ts. export/index.ts must NOT re-export schema.ts, so zod stays out of the webview bundle.

Contracts
- The types are frozen in project/types.ts, edit/types.ts, export/graphJson.ts, actions.ts, facts.ts, model.ts and markup/types.ts.
- facts.ts now has DeclFacts.typeSort and FactsStatus 'unsupported-project'; model.ts has ProofStatus.conditional.footprint.

- You also own kindChange.ts, layout.ts, paths.ts and graph.ts. They are implemented: keep their behaviour, since the integrator-owned contracts.test.ts and protocol.test.ts guard it.
- Tests read fixtures with Vite ?raw imports (test/raw-imports.d.ts), and JSON via ?raw plus JSON.parse.
- fileHashes in tests can be any strings that equal the facts' sourceSha256: core only compares them.

INPUTS
ProjectInput = parsed files (WP1's ParsedFile), sha256 per path, optional LeanFacts (facts.ts; produced by WP3 per plan section 4) and the library name.

BUILD (plan 6.1-6.5)

Binding and ids
- Bind blocks to declarations: statement = block.binding.statement.
- A pinned name falls back to resolution against the block's enclosing namespaces when there is no exact match.
- justification = <statement>.holds, from the facts or the syntactic decls.
- Resolve derived-id collisions workspace-wide by suffixing (files in path order). TL006 only for duplicated written ids.
- TL007, TL015, TL017.

Which facts (plan 6.3)
- A file is fresh when its hash matches facts.modules[].sourceSha256.
- A stale file keeps a declaration's previous facts BY NAME while its current syntactic keyword agrees with the facts' kind: flag stale, refs dropped, uses/presupposes/axioms kept.
- Otherwise, and for failed, dependency-failed or not-built modules or when there are no facts, only the syntactic keyword counts:
  - an axiom counts as an axiom;
  - a theorem counts as NOT proved: proof none plus not-checked. Never show proved without Lean.
- Anonymous instances: match facts to syntax by the declaration's start line.

Statuses (exactly per the 6.3 table)
- A justificationKind of 'other' is treated like theorem.
- Conditional vs proved: take the whitespace-normalised #check type and split it at top-level arrows.
- Footprint mapping:
  - a node's .holds becomes its id;
  - a presupposition becomes presup:<name>;
  - standard axioms and vocabulary symbols are dropped;
  - anything else becomes axiom:<name> plus TL103.
- ProofStatus.conditional also carries footprint.
- Flags:
  - rests-on-claimed, proved-goal, provable-assumption, missing-holds, uses-sorry, holds-mismatch, not-checked, stale, self-evident;
  - no-rationale: ASSUMPTION only, with TL011;
  - existence-commitment, with TL108;
  - definitional-choice.
- TL102 per 6.3.
- ill-formed = TL101, TL113, or a Lean error message inside the node's statement or .holds declaration.

Edges (plan 6.3)
- Declared edges from premises.
- VERIFIED EDGES FROM REFERENCES, not from footprints:
  - direct(v) = the nodes whose .holds v's .holds uses: follow DeclFacts.refs through declarations owned by no node until a node's .holds is reached;
  - plus conditional edges for on(v).
  - Footprints list only axioms and would miss every derivation-to-goal edge. Verified: theorem g2.holds := d0.holds.2 lists only d0's assumptions.
- lean-ref edges.
- Mismatch flags only for proved or conditional targets, at the assumption level as defined in 6.3: TL107 used-undeclared, TL109 declared-unused.
- Only edges with both ends in the subject go into subjectGraph.

Vocabulary (plan 6.4)
- sort;
- presupposition, attached to its sort;
- Nonempty instances that re-export a presupposition are hidden;
- unmarked-axiom plus TL104 when typeSort is Prop;
- predicate with arity, including 0;
- constant and function, plus TL111 when declared with axiom or when the binder types are not sorts;
- other plus TL111;
- definition, plus definitional-choice when it lies in a statement closure; untracked Prop defs are definitions too;
- lemma;
- declarations with a parent are folded into their parent.
- Syntactic fallback on the declaration text.
- Display order per 6.4; usedBy; glossBy 'user'.

Card data (plan 6.4)
- code and codeLoc: the contiguous statement-to-holds text including the docstring, or pieces joined by a blank line.
- uses: the statement's refs, then breadth-first through referenced node statements and vocabulary definitions; first occurrence wins; names from another subject are kept.
- refs:
  - refs to vocabulary items or to a node's statement/.holds, the card's own included;
  - code-relative, fresh files only;
  - all other refs dropped (e.g. And.right from .2 projections, Nat).
- presupposes, axioms, justificationKind.

Diagnostics (plan 6.5)
- TL006, TL007, TL015, TL017 and TL101-TL121.
- Lean build messages as code LEAN, with file, range and nodeId by containment.
- WP1's markup diagnostics, mapped with nodeId.
- Subjects come from paths.ts (subjectOfPath): a block outside a subject gives TL120; a premise in another subject gives TL121.
- Ids are unique workspace-wide.

subjectGraph
- Nodes ordered by orderByLayout: layout first, then file order (files sorted by path).
- The subject's edges, vocabulary and diagnostics, and the semantic summary passed in.
- For the Spyro fixture with matching facts it must reproduce spyroGraph()'s card data; for the runner-lean proved overlay with matching facts, spyroProvedGraph()'s. The review made both samples consistent with their fixtures.

PLANNING (plan 6.2, D-18)
EditPlans carry whole-file Lean FileChanges (use WP1's applyTextEdits, setBlockField and applyLeanOps), plus layout and archive. The runner materialises the sidecars.

add-node
- id = deriveId(naturalName, taken), taken over all workspace ids. preferredId is ignored in M1.
- The sentence is verbatim (trim only). asserted = ctx.today.
- The block goes into inboxPath(subject) at end-of-namespace.
- When Inbox is missing, create it with subjectScaffold's Inbox text and add import <library>.<S>.Inbox to <library>/<S>.lean if that exists, else to <library>.lean.
- Append to the layout. Set nodeId.

edit-node
- setBlockField.
- If the statement's docstring equals escapeBodyText(old natural_name) (trimmed), also emit a set-docstring LeanOp with the new sentence (D-9 mirror).
- null removes rationale, stance or source; never naturalName.

Every plan that edits a block
- whose node is formalised by adjacency also writes lean: <fully-qualified statement> (D-8 pinning);
- whose id was derived also writes id:.

delete-node
- planDelete.
- Remove the block and, unless keepLean, its statement and .holds; archive theorems as ArchiveEntry.
- Drop the id from other blocks' premises:.
- Update the layout with withoutIds.
- brokenDependents = proofs that use the removed .holds AND statements that mention the removed abbrev.
- keepLean with an axiom .holds sets leavesUnmarkedAxiom.

change-kind (planKindChange, per the 6.2 table)
- No dependents choice: needs-confirmation ActionError listing the dependents (node ids, plus the Lean names of untracked declarations).
- mark-broken: remove-holds.
- rewrite, exactly per 6.2:
  - facts-stale unless every touched file is fresh;
  - unsafe when a user is not a theorem, or, for an axiom H, when a declaration whose axioms list H is not reached through the refs;
  - hypName h_<last component of S>, made unique;
  - add-hypothesis with the binder first;
  - apply-hypothesis for the members of the closure;
  - then remove-holds.
- Move the layout with moveInLayout.
- The impact equals kindChangeImpact on the same graph; its dependents may be extended by untracked declarations.
- Optional rationale for a change to ASSUMPTION.

reorder
Layout only, layoutOnly: true.

set-premises
- Replace premises:.
- Targets must exist in the same subject, with no self-reference and no cycle (else invalid).
- Empty premises: ActionError not-yet ('Self-evident? arrives with Claude in M2').

create-subject
- The name must be valid (isSubjectName) and unused.
- subjectScaffold files.
- import <library>.<S> appended after the last import of <library>.lean (create the file if missing).
- Empty layout.

Labels: exactly per plan 6.2's list.

GRAPH.JSON (plan 6.6)
- toGraphJson is deterministic and covers all subjects.
- Generate packages/core/schema/telelean-graph-1.0.schema.json from the zod schema with z.toJSONSchema (zod 4.6.7 is installed; do NOT use ajv). For example, a vitest test that rewrites the file when UPDATE_SCHEMA=1.

- Unit-test statuses, edges, vocabulary and planning logic on hand-built ParsedFile objects. Write fixture builders; WP1's types are frozen.
- Gate text-producing tests with describe.skipIf(!isImplemented(() => parseLeanFile('X.lean', ''))).
- Write packages/core/test/fixtures/project/spyro-facts.json by hand from plan section 4 and the sample, plus a proved-overlay variant with d0/g2-style extras. Use real ilean refs, for example:

LEAN AND RAM RULES:
- Run Lean only through runLean (sandboxed, memory-capped). For quick probes on trusted fixture copies in your scratch dir you may call the toolchain binaries directly (~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.35.0/bin/lake and lean); never the elan proxies.

GOAL
Implement refreshLeanFacts(request) in packages/runner/src/semantic/.
- Types are frozen in semantic/types.ts; LeanFacts is frozen in packages/core/src/facts.ts, including the new FactsStatus 'unsupported-project' and DeclFacts.typeSort.
- Additive optional fields only, each recorded in plan section 14.

Follow plan section 4 step by step:

1. Memory guard
- readMemAvailable hook, default readMemAvailableBytes.
- Below the threshold: status low-memory, nothing spawned.

2. Toolchain and project
- lean-toolchain (trimmed) must equal leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0, else unsupported-toolchain.
- lake-manifest.json must exist and have an empty packages list, else unsupported-project with a detail.
- Nothing is spawned in either case.

3. Build
- Read and sha256 every module source (<library>.lean, <library>/**.lean) and keep the texts.
- lake build IN PLACE via runLean: shadowDir: root; maskPaths: [root/.git] only if it exists; memoryMax, timeouts, runId and signal passed through.

4. Parse Lake's log, using the verified line shapes of plan 4 step 4:
- progress lines (Built, Replayed, Building) with the check marks;
- trace lines are ignored;
- messages are kept whole, continuation lines included;
- the 'Some required targets logged failures:' list gives the failed modules.
- Convert Lean's 1-based line and 0-based code-point column to a 0-based line and UTF-16 character, using the step-3 text. Ranges are zero-width.

5. Module states
- fresh, failed, dependency-failed, not-built, stale.
- Imports come from the source headers. Lake deletes a failed module's .olean/.ilean.

6. Read .ilean
- Path: .lake/build/lib/lean/<Module/Path>.ilean, version 5. The exact shape is in plan 4 step 6:
  - decls: name to [full range, selection range];
  - references: keyed by a JSON string {c:{m,n}}, with definition (4 or 5 elements) and usages [l,c,l,c,parent].
- Skip _private. names.
- Set parent for auxiliary names (structure fields).

7. The check file
Generated, on stdin to lake env lean --stdin --json, via runLean.
- Import only fresh modules: never failed, dependency-failed or not-built ones, even if old .olean files exist. With no fresh module, the check is skipped.
- set_option pp.fullNames true and pp.proofs false.
- Per declaration: #check @N, #print N and #print axioms N; for axioms and opaques also #check type_of% @N.
- Names are written with M0's formatDeclName.
- Messages are attributed by 1-based line, as M0's footprintsFromMessages does.
Extract:
- type: the text after the first ' : ', with whitespace runs collapsed to one space (long types wrap);
- kind and attributes from #print. kind is instance when the declaration's source text, after docstring, attributes and modifiers, starts with the instance keyword: Lean prints Prop instances as theorem and data instances as @[instance_reducible] def;
- value for defs (after :=);
- axioms (M0 parseAxiomsMessage, multi-line) and usesSorry;
- typeSort: the text after the last ' : ' of the type_of% output;
- error.

8. Docstrings
From the source, at each decl's full range.

9. Re-hash
Re-hash the sources and mark changed modules stale.

REUSE AND CONSTRAINTS
- Reuse the M0 helpers in packages/runner/src/lean: runLean, toolchainExe, resolveToolchain, parseLeanJsonMessages, parseAxiomsMessage, formatDeclName.
- Keep all M0 lean tests passing. You may refactor lean/ (you own it), but keep its exports.
- You may export internal helpers (check-file generator, ilean reader, log parser) from semantic/index.ts.
- refreshLeanFacts never throws for Lean or sandbox failures (statuses with details).
- It is not self-serialising: callers use runExclusive.

FIXTURES
New overlays go in test-fixtures/semantic/, applied over scratch copies of test-fixtures/spyro:
(a) a build error in Main;
(b) the runner-lean proved overlay plus extras:
  - a conditional theorem 'theorem d1.holds (h : cynder_not_good) : d1';
  - a long-named two-hypothesis conditional whose #check output wraps;
  - a derivation used by a proof ('theorem d0.holds' and 'theorem g2.holds : g2 := d0.holds.2');
  - a proof through an untracked lemma;
  - a sorry theorem;
  - a hidden axiom 'axiom hidden : ∀ c : Character, HasDarkPast c';
  - 'axiom c2 : Character', 'axiom P0 : Prop', 'axiom f : Character → Game';
  - a def used by a statement abbrev;
  - a structure with a field;
  - a data instance;
(c) an edited lean-toolchain;
(d) a lake-manifest.json listing a package, and a copy with the manifest removed;
(e) a non-BMP character before an erroring identifier on one line.
The review probed most of these on Lean 4.35; the outputs are quoted in plan section 4. Fixtures are plain trusted .lean files with no #eval, and contain no .telelean/config.json.

RUN
cd packages/runner && TELELEAN_TEST_TMP=<scratch> npx vitest run test/semantic, then the full suite once (about 70 s for M0).
Report the files, the real test output, measured durations and peak memory, contract additions, and effects outside the repo (units left, known-projects line count).

MODEL WORKSPACE (plan 2, 3)

load()
- Lists <library>.lean, <library>/**.lean and .telelean/subjects/*/layout.json via fs (skip dot-dirs, .lake and node_modules).
- Reads the texts through the TextSource, sha256-hashes them and parses them with core parseLeanFile.
- The library comes from .telelean/config.json via parseProjectConfig.

graph(subject)
- Cache parses by path plus hash.
- graph(subject) = core subjectGraph(buildProjectModel(...)), with the subject's layout and the current SemanticSummary.
- Its version counter is seeded from Date.now() and strictly increasing, across subjects and across workspaces re-created in one process.
- An unknown subject throws.

invalidate and events
- invalidate re-reads; a file that is now null is removed.
- onDidChange events.

requestRefresh
- Debounce (750 ms default), coalesce, and run one at a time per process via semantic.runExclusive(() => refreshLeanFacts({root, library, memoryMax, minAvailableBytes, onPhase, ...})).
- The refreshFacts option is the test hook.
- The semantic state is 'checking' while it runs.
- Map FactsStatus to SemanticSummary per plan section 4 (unsupported-project becomes disabled plus a TL201 diagnostic).
- Keep the previous facts after a failed refresh.
- Rewrite .telelean/graph.json (core toGraphJson; direct fs write; gitignored) after each refresh and each perform.
- refreshNow().

perform(action)
Refusals (ActionError) become {ok:false, code, error, dependents?} outcomes, never a throw.
1. core planAction(model, action, {today, now, layouts}).
2. Materialise sidecars into whole-file FileChanges: layout.json via serializeLayout; attic entries appended to atticPath(subject, nodeId) with the header '-- archived <ISO time> (<reason>): <declName>'.
3. A 'Manual edits' snapshot of each touched scope whose current files differ from its tip.
4. EditApplier.apply(changes, label). It rejects when a file's current text differs from before: report conflict.
5. The action snapshot of each touched scope: subject chains via subjectSnapshotScope, the project chain via projectSnapshotScope. Skip it when layoutOnly.
6. Push the undo entry and clear redo.
7. invalidate plus requestRefresh.
Serialise perform, undo, redo, revert and prune in one queue.

UNDO (plan 8)
- Per subject, in memory, at most 100 entries.
- Exact reversal when current === after.
- Otherwise, reverse patches with the installed diff 9.0.0 (structuredPatch/applyPatch, no fuzz).
- A file the action created is deleted only if unchanged.
- All or nothing: refuse with conflict ('<file> changed since; use History to revert').
- Undo and redo are applied like actions, snapshotted 'Undo: <label>' / 'Redo: <label>', and are themselves undoable.
- A subject that disappears (undo of create-subject) leaves subjects() without it.

HISTORY (plan 8, exact rules)
- Refs: refs/telelean/<rootKey>/subjects/<S> and .../project. rootKey per the plan; validate with check-ref-format.
- A snapshot is a commit of exactly the scope's files, with paths relative to the model root and contents from the TextSource.
- Build it with plumbing only:
  - hash-object -w;
  - then a temporary index file in a fresh temp dir (GIT_INDEX_FILE), or mktree;
  - write-tree;
  - commit-tree with the trailers Telelean-Action, Telelean-Subject, Telelean-Nodes and Telelean-Format;
  - update-ref with the old value.
- Every git call: -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c gc.auto=0 -c core.fsmonitor=false; env GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; author and committer 'telelean <telelean@localhost>' via env.
- Never touch the user's index, HEAD, branches or hooks.
- 'Initial state' when a subject chain is missing (on load or board open).
- listHistory: newest first, plus storage from git rev-list --objects --disk-usage <ref> --not --branches --tags --remotes, per subject and over all of the root's refs, cached for 10 s.
- historyDiff: parent or current, as a FileChange list.
- revert:
  - snapshot the current state if it is dirty;
  - write the entry's tree over the subject scope (create/replace/delete) through the EditApplier, labelled 'Revert to: <label> (<time>)';
  - snapshot it and make it undoable.
- prune(keepLast): recreate the last N commits with the same trees, messages and dates (the oldest becomes a root commit) and update the ref. No gc.
- historyStatus: ready, no-repo, git-missing, disabled or error.
- initGit: initGitRepository (refuses inside an existing repository; git init only, no commit to any branch), then the initial snapshots.
- Labels per plan 6.2.

INITIALIZE (plan 7.1, 7.2)

inspectFolder
- empty: hidden files and .git only; record the .gitignore text.
- model: has .telelean/config.json.
- lake-project: lakefile.toml with a [[lean_lib]] name, lake-manifest.json with no packages, and no [[require]]. subjects = the library's subdirectories with subject names. Record the .gitignore text.
- unsupported, with a reason: lakefile.lean only; no [[lean_lib]]; no manifest; Lake dependencies such as Mathlib; other files without a lakefile.
