work_packages.brief:
Read docs/m1-plan.md first: the safety rules at the top, and sections 1.3, 5.1, 5.5, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 7.3, 8, 10, 12 (R5), 13, 14 and 15.

SAFETY (mandatory; also for anything you start):
- Never push, add remotes or use gh.
- Never publish or send anything to anyone.
- Network only to read docs.
- No downloads, no npm install, no new packages. Report a need in open issues.
- Never run the Claude CLI with a prompt. Never read credentials.
- Write only inside your owned paths and your scratch dir /tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn9/<your-label>/.
- Never touch the user's VS Code settings or extensions, ~/telelean_scripts, ~/.config, ~/.claude, ~/.elan, the npm config or the global git config.
- No sudo, no global installs. Do not run git in /home/zhengyew/telelean.
- Kill only processes you started.
- Report every effect outside the repo. Never claim a test passed unless you ran it; quote real output.

CHROME RULES:
- Playwright uses the installed Chrome (no browser download), one worker, an isolated HOME/XDG (plan 10) and ulimit -c 0.
- Do not run the VS Code smoke test (it is WP5's).
- Run free -m before running Chrome and wait while MemAvailable is under 12 GB.

GOAL
The M1 board in React 19 plus zustand, built by Vite into packages/extension/dist/webview.
- It consumes only @telelean/core:
  - protocol (frozen; do not edit);
  - model types;
  - kindChangeImpact and proofDependents (implemented);
  - samples (frozen): spyroGraph, spyroProvedGraph and largeGraph carry the M1 card data; spyroProvedGraph now matches the runner-lean proved overlay. Build variants for other statuses in your tests.
- Keep the M0 strict CSP:
  - no inline style attributes;
  - use the CSSOM, CSS classes and --vscode-* variables;
  - give fallbacks for the new contributed colours --vscode-telelean-vocabulary and --vscode-telelean-highlight.

STORE
- Handle all host messages:
  - graph: drop a graph whose version is lower than the last applied one; re-applying the same version is harmless;
  - workspace, history, actionResult, notice.
- Mutations carry a requestId (r<n>).
- Optimistic updates for drag, add and reorder roll back on actionResult ok:false, with an error toast.
- An add's optimistic card (provisional id) is replaced when the graph arrives; outcome.nodeId moves its selection and expansion to the final id.
- A needs-confirmation result opens the dependents dialog with outcome.dependents: node ids are shown as their sentences, other entries as Lean names in mono.
- addNode sends the sentence trimmed only (verbatim, D-16). Pasted line breaks become spaces, since the protocol requires one line.

UI

1. VOCABULARY GROUP at the top of the Assumptions list
- Collapsible. The state is kept in the webview state via setState, per board; not in layout.json.
- Grouped:
  - Types;
  - Predicates & relations;
  - Functions;
  - Constants;
  - Presuppositions: chips such as 'assumes characters exist', made from the sort's gloss ('assumes <gloss> exist'), falling back to 'assumes there is a <shortName>';
  - Definitions;
  - Lemmas;
  - Unmarked axioms (warning);
  - Other.
- Box-shaped items show the shortName, the type (mono) and the gloss (italic, with a marker if glossBy is 'agent').
- Each item is highlightable: scroll it into view within the column, plus a ~2 s data-highlight flash.

2. CARD FACE (M0 plus)
- Aura and a proof chip for every ProofStatus kind and flag:
  - pending-promotion: 'promotion pending';
  - conditional: 'conditional on …';
  - proved-goal: 'proved: make Derivation?';
  - uses-sorry; missing-holds;
  - not-checked: 'not checked by Lean', never a check mark;
  - stale: a subtle 'checking…' marker over the last known status.
- One 'needs attention' badge counting the error/warning diagnostics for the node.
- A D-13 hint chip on an ASSUMPTION with declared premises: 'you think this follows from those: prove it?'.
- A 'uses:' line when lean.uses exists:
  - deterministic truncation: the first 2 short names, then ', …' when there are more;
  - a toggle '▾ N' opens a dropdown listing all of them with kind and gloss; names from another subject are shown fully qualified;
  - clicking an entry highlights the vocabulary item.

3. EXPANDED VIEW
- The Lean code in a pre with class tl-lean.
  - Request 1: a drag inside it must select text and never drag the card. CSS alone cannot do this in Chrome (plan R5).
  - On pointerdown inside the code, set the card's draggable attribute to false; restore it on pointerup, pointercancel or blur.
  - Also: canDrag false for drags starting in the code; draggable=false and user-select:text on the code.
  - Clicks in the code do not toggle card selection: stop propagation; a click that ends a text selection changes nothing.
- Identifiers covered by lean.refs are spans:
  - hover shows a tooltip element with the gloss (vocabulary) or the sentence (node refs);
  - a plain click highlights the vocabulary item, or, for nodeId refs, reveals and flashes that card;
  - Ctrl/Cmd+click is reserved (no action yet).
- A Copy button posts copyText with exactly lean.code.
- An 'Open in editor' button posts openInEditor with codeLoc or loc.
- Footprint (proved and conditional) and presuppositions lists.
- 'Depends on' and 'Used by' lists (03 section 7; also the keyboard route). Each entry is clickable to reveal and flash its card.
  - Depends on: declared premises, verified sources, and statement mentions from lean-ref edges.
  - Used by: nodes declaring it, proofs using it (via proofDependents), and statements mentioning it.
- Buttons 'Make Assumption/Derivation/Goal' (the keyboard/menu equivalent of the drop zones, with the same impact and dialog), Edit, Delete.

4. INLINE EDIT
The sentence, the rationale ('because:' line), and the stance/source chips post editNode. Enter saves, Escape cancels; an empty rationale removes it.

5. DELETE DIALOG
- Lists the nodes that declare it as a premise (declared edges), the proofs that use it (proofDependents) and the statements that mention it (lean-ref edges).
- Options:
  - 'Delete card and its Lean code' (default);
  - 'Delete card only, keep Lean', explaining the hidden-assumption consequence;
  - Cancel.
- Posts deleteNode.

6. DRAG
- Within a column: post reorder (M0 posted nothing).
- Across columns, the drop zones show kindChangeImpact(graph, id, to).summary.
- On drop:
  - needsConfirmation opens the dialog: the dependents; 'Rewrite them to take it as a hypothesis' (disabled unless rewriteAvailable); 'Keep them, marked broken'; Cancel;
  - asksRationale shows an optional 'Why do you hold it?' field (Skip allowed);
  - then post kindChange with dependents/rationale.

7. A|D|G BOX
- Stance chips for Assumption: I believe it / It's a rule or definition / Supposing, for argument.
- A why field whose placeholder follows the stance and kind:
  - 'Why do you believe it?' / 'Where does the rule come from?' / 'What are you exploring?';
  - Derivation: 'Why do you think it follows?';
  - Goal: 'Why do you care?'.
- Optional source chips: observed / reported / inferred / common knowledge.
- Posts addNode with rationale, stance and source.

8. TRAY
- Presupposition chips from lean.presupposes of the selected nodes.
- 'These suffice ▶' posts theseSuffice.
- With zero premises, a disabled 'Self-evident?' plus the note 'available with Claude in M2'.

9. HEADER
- Subject picker: workspace.subjects with counts; 'New subject…' inline, with isSubjectName validation, posts createSubject; selecting posts selectSubject.
- History dropdown:
  - posts historyList on open;
  - entries 'time · action · label';
  - storage text 'This subject: 12 KB · All subjects: 30 KB';
  - per entry: Preview (historyPreview, compare parent) and 'Revert to this' (confirm, then historyRevert);
  - 'Keep last N' posts historyPrune;
  - when history.state is no-repo, an 'Initialize git' button posts initGit;
  - messages for git-missing, disabled and error.
- Lean badge per SemanticSummary state (plan section 4 mapping); clicking it posts refresh.
- A problems list (diagnostics); file items post openInEditor.
- The syntactic-mode banner for unsupported-toolchain, and the detail for disabled.
- Undo/redo buttons with the workspace labels.
- The M0 legend, extended with the conditional and mismatch arrows.

10. EDGES
- Declared dashed, verified solid (M0).
- Conditional verified edges are solid, with a distinct marker and a 'taken as a hypothesis' tooltip.
- Mismatch edges in a warning colour, with a tooltip.
- lean-ref edges are drawn thin, only while one end is hovered or selected.

11. TOASTS AND KEYS
- Toasts from notice; an Undo button when undoable posts undo.
- Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (and Ctrl+Y) on the board post undo/redo when focus is not in an input, textarea or contenteditable.

HARNESS (test/harness/harness.js)
- Reply to mutations with actionResult ok (outcome.nodeId for addNode).
- Answer historyList with a canned listing.
- Let tests inject host messages: workspace, notice, and actionResult failures including needs-confirmation.

PLAYWRIGHT CONFIG
- In playwright.config.ts, launchOptions.env gets HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME inside the run's short temp dir.
- Args: --disable-crash-reporter --disable-breakpad --no-first-run.
- The test:e2e script is sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; playwright test'.
- Compare the real ~/.config/google-chrome listing before and after.

Update M0 tests whose expectations the plan changed (e.g. reorder now posts) and say so.

RUN
cd packages/webview && npm test (typecheck, build into dist/webview, unit, e2e).
Report the files, the real test output, the before/after home-dir listings and open issues for frozen files.

AT6.21 For spyroProvedGraph, the expanded card's Depends on / Used by lists are right (the goal depends on the three assumptions; cynder-dark-past is used by the goal), and each entry reveals its card. The legend shows the declared, verified, conditional and mismatch arrows and the aura

minor_decisions.decision: The per-card vocabulary ('uses:'), hover glosses and click targets come from Lake's .ilean files (v5: declaration ranges, and references with their parent declarations). Kind, type, statement value, footprint and sorry come from a generated check file (#check @N, #print N, #print axioms N, plus #check type_of% @N for axioms and opaques, with pp.fullNames and pp.proofs false). No compiled extractor and no import Lean in M1.
minor_decisions.rationale: Verified on Lean 4.35 by the architect and the review: exact resolved references, with UTF-16 columns; about 0.3 s and 480 MB for the check. This keeps 03 §5's tool-free M1. The toolchain is pinned, so the internal format is stable, and unknown versions degrade to 'no refs'.

minor_decisions.decision: The Lean refresh builds in place in the model folder (sources read-only, .lake writable, .git masked), not in a shadow. A module is fresh unless Lake failed it or one of its imports failed; Lake deletes failed modules' .olean/.ilean. Sources are hashed before and after the build, to mark stale files.
minor_decisions.rationale: This matches 03 §8.4/D-24 and is incremental and fast. Staleness keyed by file hash is 03 §2 step 3. The review corrected the risk note: Lake has no build lock, so races with the user's Lean server are possible but self-healing; a private build shadow is the fallback.

minor_decisions.decision: The opt-in marker is .telelean/config.json (it also holds the library name), not layout.json.
minor_decisions.rationale: Layout is per subject and optional; a dedicated config file is a clearer marker and holds the project settings.

minor_decisions.decision: Sidecars are per subject: .telelean/subjects/<S>/layout.json and attic/<id>.lean. graph.json stays at the root (gitignored).
minor_decisions.rationale: A subject's history snapshot and revert then cover exactly its own files (D-10 plus A3's per-subject counter).

minor_decisions.decision: History uses one git ref chain per subject (refs/telelean/<rootKey>/subjects/<S>) plus a project chain, built with plumbing only (temporary index, commit-tree, update-ref). Every call uses -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c gc.auto=0 -c core.fsmonitor=false, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and an explicit author.
minor_decisions.rationale: Revert stays per subject; the storage counter is per subject and overall; the user's index, branches and hooks are never touched, as D-33/A3 promised. fsmonitor is off so a user-configured monitor daemon is never started.

minor_decisions.decision: Layout-only changes (re-order) are undoable but not snapshotted on their own.
minor_decisions.rationale: Layout carries no meaning, and an entry per drag would flood the history the user wants for meta-analysis.

minor_decisions.decision: 'Keep last N' rewrites the chain and does not run git gc on the user's repository.
minor_decisions.rationale: Running gc or prune on the user's repo is invasive. The counter (reachable objects) drops at once, and the disk space returns at git's next housekeeping.

minor_decisions.decision: mental_model/ is written without .lake and without git init. The board offers 'Initialize git' when the user wants history there.
minor_decisions.rationale: mental_model sits inside /home/zhengyew/telelean, which must stay git-free; git init is the user's choice (Initialize offers it).

minor_decisions.decision: In M1, 'These suffice' writes the target's premises: (declared support, D-13) and says that proving with Claude arrives in M2. Zero premises ('Self-evident?') answers 'available from M2'.
minor_decisions.rationale: M1 has no AI; the button still does what D-13 defines for it. Self-evidence is meaningful only with a run.

minor_decisions.decision: Strict D-2(b): a block bound to anything other than a Prop abbrev/def is flagged TL113 (ill-formed). The message says how to write the approved form.
minor_decisions.rationale: telelean writes and reads only the approved convention; guessing other shapes would make statuses unreliable.

minor_decisions.decision: 'uses:' is the vocabulary in the statement closure: the statement's own refs, then refs reached through other nodes' statements and through vocabulary definitions, in first-occurrence order; sorts appear only where written. Inline it shows the first 2 names, then ', …', with a '▾ N' dropdown.
minor_decisions.rationale: This follows the user's 'HasDarkPast, cynder, ...' example deterministically (so it is testable) and works for large vocabularies. Going through definitions shows what the meaning really depends on (D-4).

minor_decisions.decision: Clicking another node's name inside the expanded code reveals and flashes that card, besides the requested vocabulary highlight. Ctrl+click is reserved for later.
minor_decisions.rationale: A natural extension of the user's hover/click idea at the same cost; it keeps Ctrl+click free for their planned go-to/edit features.

minor_decisions.decision: Glosses are shown as the user's wording in M1 (glossBy 'user'); M2 marks agent-worded docstrings.
minor_decisions.rationale: There is no agent in M1; D-3's 'Claude's wording until you rewrite it' matters only once runs create vocabulary.

minor_decisions.decision: Instances that only re-export a presupposition (instance : Nonempty T := T.exists) are not listed in the vocabulary group.
minor_decisions.rationale: They are plumbing for the presupposition chip and would clutter the group. The review found that Lean prints them as theorems, so they are recognised by the source keyword and matched by start line.

minor_decisions.decision: wording.jsonl and attempts.jsonl are not written in M1.
minor_decisions.rationale: History snapshots keep every old wording; attempts only exist once runs exist (M2).

minor_decisions.decision: The graph.json JSON Schema is generated from a zod schema (z.toJSONSchema) kept out of the webview bundle.
minor_decisions.rationale: zod is a declared, installed dependency; ajv is present only transitively and may not be added.

minor_decisions.decision: The runner is typecheck-only (noEmit). Runner and extension resolve @telelean/core (and the extension also @telelean/runner) from source, through tsconfig paths and vitest aliases.
minor_decisions.rationale: The extension and webview already work this way; no build step or workspace links are needed, and stale dist output is avoided.

minor_decisions.decision: Applying an edit saves the touched files, including any unsaved typing in them. The applier first refuses if a file changed since the plan was made.
minor_decisions.rationale: D-17 says edits are saved immediately, and history and undo need the result on disk. The before-check prevents overwriting typing that arrives between planning and applying.

minor_decisions.decision: New-subject import order: Vocabulary ← Inbox ← Main (Main imports Inbox).
minor_decisions.rationale: Nodes formalised by hand in Inbox can then be used by Main without moving code.

minor_decisions.decision: No port-drag arrows in M1. The expanded card has 'Make Assumption/Derivation/Goal' buttons as the keyboard and menu equivalent of the drop zones.
minor_decisions.rationale: The tray already declares support; the buttons give accessibility and testability with the same impact/dialog logic.

minor_decisions.decision: Contributed colour ids keep exactly one dot and get explicit per-theme hex defaults (no charts.*); telelean.vocabulary and telelean.highlight are added.
minor_decisions.rationale: M0 lessons: VS Code replaces only the first dot, and some themes derive charts.* badly.

minor_decisions.decision: Parts of the contract were implemented up front so builders need not wait: by the architect, the protocol validators, kindChangeImpact, the layout/path helpers, runExclusive and readMemAvailableBytes; by the review, subjectScaffold with frozen exact texts.
minor_decisions.rationale: The webview can build and test drop zones and messages without the host. Initialize, New subject and the sample write identical files without WP2 and WP4 coordinating.

minor_decisions.decision: requestId is optional on all mutating messages (actionResult only when one is given); theseSuffice accepts empty premises.
minor_decisions.rationale: The M0 webview keeps compiling and its tests stay valid during the parallel build, and it leaves room for M2's self-evident runs.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Verified arrows come from Lean's references (the proof's .ilean usages, followed through untracked lemmas to the first node). Footprints still come from #print axioms.
minor_decisions.rationale: #print axioms lists only axioms (verified: theorem g2.holds := d0.holds.2 lists only d0's assumptions). Footprint-based arrows would miss every derivation→goal edge, and D→G could then delete a .holds another proof uses, which D-11 forbids.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Declared-vs-verified mismatches (TL107/TL109) are judged at the assumption level, and only for proved or conditional targets.
minor_decisions.rationale: A proof that routes through a derivation of the declared premises should not be flagged, and an unproved goal's premises are never 'unused'.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) A stale file keeps its previous facts by name while the declaration keyword is unchanged (flag stale). Theorems that Lean has not checked show no proof (not-checked) instead of the syntactic 'proved'.
minor_decisions.rationale: Statuses don't flicker while typing, and the board never claims 'proved' without Lean (the prototype's integrity principle).

minor_decisions.decision: (review) The mechanical D-11 rewrite inserts the hypothesis as the first binder, and refuses (unsafe) when a dependent is not a theorem or a use is invisible to the references.
minor_decisions.rationale: With the binder last, (c h) passes h to the wrong parameter for theorems that have their own hypotheses. A def cannot take a hypothesis without changing its type. 'Mark broken' stays available.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Projects with Lake dependencies (e.g. Mathlib) are refused in M1: Initialize returns unsupported, and the refresh returns unsupported-project without spawning anything.
minor_decisions.rationale: D-28 asks for an explicit Mathlib opt-in (M4), and building or importing Mathlib would break the user's RAM rule.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Hidden assumptions are recognised by Lean's sort check (#check type_of% @N prints ': Prop'), not by guessing from the type text. An axiom-declared constant or function is flagged TL111.
minor_decisions.rationale: Verified output on 4.35. An axiom constant asserts existence without the visible presupposition D-3 requires; opaque constants make it explicit.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) An adjacent binding is pinned (lean: written) on the next telelean edit of its block, like the derived-id write-back (D-8).
minor_decisions.rationale: D-8 says telelean pins once a node is formalised; in M1 the user formalises by hand, so the next edit is the natural moment.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) The host always derives new node ids itself (deriveId, with n-<hex> for non-Latin text). The webview's provisional id only matches its optimistic card.
minor_decisions.rationale: The webview's slug and core's deriveId differ for non-Latin sentences (D-8 requires the n-<hex> fallback). ActionOutcome.nodeId tells the webview the final id.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) The M0 legend gains the conditional and mismatch arrows. The expanded card gets 'Depends on / Used by' lists. An ASSUMPTION with declared premises shows D-13's 'prove it?' hint.
minor_decisions.rationale: D-15 requires a legend; 03 §7 specifies the Depends on/Used by buttons (also the keyboard and screen-reader route); D-13 specifies the hint. All are cheap in M1.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) The vocabulary group's collapsed state is kept in the webview state (per board, survives reloads), not in layout.json.
minor_decisions.rationale: Writing a file per toggle would create undo entries and file churn for UI state.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) A model workspace is created when its first board opens and lives until the window closes; Lean refreshes run only while a board is open.
minor_decisions.rationale: Undo survives closing and reopening the board; parsing is cheap; D-28's refresh rule is kept.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) spyroProvedGraph() was corrected to match test-fixtures/runner-lean/overlays/proved: block locs, pg-no-dark-past pinned, its docstring line in code, codeLoc 13-15.
minor_decisions.rationale: The sample is the canonical card data that WP2 and the integrator reproduce from real facts; it must agree with the fixture it cites.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Core tests read fixture files with Vite ?raw imports, declared once in packages/core/test/raw-imports.d.ts.
minor_decisions.rationale: Core is typechecked with types: [] on purpose (no Node APIs in src), so node:fs is unavailable in its tests; ?raw works under vitest 5 (verified).

minor_decisions.decision: (review) Lean messages keep their continuation lines. Lake log ranges are zero-width at the reported start.
minor_decisions.rationale: An M0 open item: first-line-only errors lose the detail the problems list needs. Lake prints only a start position.

minor_decisions.decision: (review) The delete dialog and planDelete also list statements that mention the node's abbrev.
minor_decisions.rationale: Deleting the statement abbrev breaks those statements too, not only proofs that use the .holds.

effects_outside_repo: Ran one read-only git command in the scratch dir: git -C <scratch>/scaffold status, which reported 'not a git repository'. No other git commands; none in /home/zhengyew/telelean.

npm wrote a debug log to ~/.npm/_logs for each of my npm/npx invocations (about 19 runs between 11:33 and 11:46 +0800, 2026-11-01): npm test, npx tsc, npx vitest and one npm config get logs-max. npm keeps only 10 logs (logs-max 10), so its rotation deleted older log files there, including logs from earlier agents' runs.

# M0 report: spikes (2026-11-01)

**Verdict: M0 is complete.** All three spikes work on this machine, each was checked by an independent verifier and then fixed, and the real-Claude smoke test passed. Nothing is usable as a tool yet; M1 is the first usable milestone (the board on your real Lean files, without AI).

## What exists now

```
packages/core       types, versioned board⇄extension protocol, Spyro sample graph (15 tests)
packages/runner     lean/  runLean sandbox, shadow copy, #print-axioms footprints, lake comparator   (140 tests,
                    llm/   provider interface, Claude CLI backend, MCP tool server, path guard, fake  lean + llm)
packages/webview    React board (24 unit tests + 13 Playwright tests in your Chrome)
packages/extension  VS Code extension "telelean: Open Board" (4 unit + 5 smoke tests in VS Code 1.140 under xvfb)
scripts/smoke-claude.mjs   the live smoke test (run once, with your permission)
test-fixtures/      the verified Spyro Lean project + inert probe files (*.lean.txt)
```

All 201 tests passed in my final re-run, done separately from the agents' own runs.

## Spike 1: sandboxed Lean runs

| Claim | Evidence (ran) |
|---|---|
| Builds run in a memory-capped bwrap sandbox | Spyro builds in ~0.9 s, peak 95 MiB; a rebuild from a copied `.lake/build` recompiles 0 modules |
| The sandbox blocks your home folder and the network | Inert probes: writing to the real `$HOME` fails; listing `$HOME` shows an empty tmpfs; DNS, TCP, D-Bus and abstract sockets are all blocked |
| The memory cap works | 600 MB allocated under a 256 MB cap is reported as `oom` (cgroup `oom_kill=1` and systemd `Result=oom-kill` agree) |
| Nothing survives a timeout, cancel or crash | The whole scope is killed in each case, including when the host process dies |
| `#print axioms` footprints are exact | `cynder_not_good.holds` has exactly the 11 expected axioms |
| `lake comparator` runs under the sandbox | Honest proof: accepted. Rejected: weakened goal (both ways), unselected assumption, smuggled axiom, `sorry`, retyped assumption, missing proof, vocabulary turned into a definition. A sandbox start-up failure is reported as "could not start", never as "rejected" |
| No side effects | `~/.elan/known-projects` stays at 36 lines; no units or processes are left over |

## Spike 2: the Claude CLI harness (your D-23(a) choice)

**Offline (93 tests):**
- argv assembly;
- environment sanitising: every `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC_*` variable is stripped, because a Claude-enabled VS Code exports parent-session variables;
- parsing of the JSON event stream;
- the loopback MCP tool server (bearer token; Host/Origin checks);
- the path guard;
- the fake backend.

**Live smoke test, on Haiku 5.5:**
- **8 requests;** about 36k cache-read, 9k cache-write and 14 uncached input tokens, and 1.1k output tokens. The CLI's cost estimate is **$0.003**.
- **(a) Login and long waits: pass.** The subscription (Claude Ultra, first-party, no API key) was verified *before* any prompt was sent. The shell tool was absent and telelean's tools loaded. A question blocked for **75 s** and the answer still reached Claude.
- **(b) File confinement: pass.**
  - Allowed: reading the model file.
  - Denied: `/etc/hostname`, a decoy file outside the copy, and whole-folder Grep/Glob, which would have searched hidden files.
  - No hidden or outside content leaked.
- **(c) Reload: pass.** The CLI was killed mid-question, then `--resume` continued the same session and finished.

## Spike 3: the board in a real VS Code webview

The board has:
- three independently scrolling columns, with each card's sentence first, a kind glyph, a blue aura when formalised, and a chevron that expands to the Lean code;
- SVG arrows: dashed for declared, solid for verified. They follow scrolling and resizing, and become a stub plus an "n linked" badge when one end is scrolled away;
- drag to another column, which requests a kind change;
- click and Ctrl/Cmd-click selection, with a tray holding a target slot and a **These suffice** button;
- the A|D|G box.

Colours come only from VS Code theme variables, and the Content Security Policy is strict and nonce-based. In the real VS Code 1.140 test instance the webview loads with **0 CSP violations** and reports "4 cards, 3 arrows" for Spyro and "75 cards, 34 arrows (31 stubs)" for the large test graph.

## Design changes learned in M0 (to fold into M1/M2)

1. **Sandbox:**
   - Add a small *keeper* process with `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`. Without it a crashed host leaves the sandbox running; this was tested as a negative control.
   - Set `OOMPolicy=stop` and run `reset-failed` afterwards.
   - "Could not start" is decided by bwrap's `exit-code` record, not by `child-pid`.
   - PATH must put the toolchain's `bin/` first, never elan's proxies.
2. **Comparator messages.** A weakened goal abbrev is reported as "definition mismatch" against the abbrev's own name. The user- and LLM-facing message should say "a definition the frozen statement depends on changed".
3. **Claude CLI:**
   - Telelean's MCP tools need `alwaysLoad` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, otherwise they hide behind a ToolSearch tool that isn't allowed.
   - Long questions need a per-server MCP timeout.
   - The account check uses the CLI's `initialize` reply before any prompt, so a refusal costs nothing.
   - In `-p` mode the CLI silently ignores an invalid settings file. Telelean therefore asks the running CLI for its hook list and refuses to start without the guard. The minimum CLI version is 2.1.295.
   - `--max-turns` counts per user turn, so telelean enforces its own run cap.
   - Haiku 5.5 can't switch thinking off in CLI 2.1.314; low effort keeps output short.
4. **Grep/Glob search hidden files.** The guard scans the search folder first. M1's shadow layout should give Claude a root holding only model files, with `.lake/` and `.telelean/` visible only inside the Lean sandbox.
5. **Board:**
   - Contributed colour ids must have exactly one do

# Design amendments (turn 2, 2026-11-01)

These amend `verbatim_prompt_log/bundle_1/user_requested_documents/02_design_decisions.md` and `03_architecture.md`, and take precedence where they conflict. The ★ recommendations were approved with the notes below.

## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface

**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.

**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.

**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.

**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.

**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).

**Traded away:**
- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.

**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

## A2 · The gate loop (your proposal, adopted)

1. Claude says it is finished.
2. Telelean runs **non-LLM checks** on Claude's working copy. Each must hold:
   - the files build in the sandbox;
   - `#print axioms` lists only your selected assumptions, plus the "X exists" presuppositions of the things they mention;
   - there is no `sorry`;
   - the goal statement is identical to the one frozen before proving (via `lake comparator`);
   - there are no forbidden commands (`#eval` etc.);
   - your natural-language text is untouched.
3. **On failure** the board shows a small notice. For example: *"Attempt 1 didn't pass: it used `foo`, which you didn't select. Asking Claude to retry."* Claude is re-prompted automatically with the exact failure.
4. **After 3 failed attempts**, a setting you can change, the board tells you what kept failing. It then **reverts the working copy to the last state that passed**. The attempt is kept in the history.

Your real files are never touched until you press Accept, so "revert" only ever applies to Claude's copy.

**What is a question for you, not a retry.** These need your judgement, which a program can't supply:
- a new definition or vocabulary item (yes/no);
- a proposed missing premise (a ghost node: "I hold this" / "no");
- whether the Lean says what your sentence says (the meaning review).

**The honest limit.** The checks guarantee that the goal follows from the selected assumptions *as formalised*. Whether the formalisation matches your meaning is what the review step (and M3's faithfulness tools) is for.

**Storage.** Every change telelean writes is first snapshotted as a private git ref in the model folder (`refs/telelean/…`); your branches are never touched. Git stores files compressed and deduplicated, so a snapshot costs only what changed, typically a few KB.

**The dropdown** (board header):
- Each entry shows time · action · one-line summary, e.g. *"These suffice → proved cynder-not-good"*.
- Selecting an entry previews that state read-only, with its diff.
- **Revert to this** first snapshots the current state, so a revert can itself be undone.

**The counter** shows disk use per subject and in total. It measures **disk, not RAM**: snapshots sit on disk and add nothing to memory pressure. A "keep the last N" pruning option is included.

**When:** M1, together with the board's first writes.

D-10 is attempted in M1: one module subtree and namespace per subject, plus a subject picker. If it proves complex, M1 ships one subject first. Comparing models, your two-person "convince someone" setting, is deferred and may need its own analyses.

## Prototype profile (personal use): what the first versions include, and what is deferred

*Added after your mid-turn prompt 5.* telelean is a prototype for your own use, and Claude is a cooperative assistant, not an attacker. Most of the security detail that the review rounds surfaced therefore matters only against a deliberately misbehaving model, or for a tool shared with others. The prototype (M1–M2) keeps only what makes the tool's central claim true, plus safety that costs almost nothing. The central claim is: **"proved" means proved from exactly the assumptions you selected.**

**Kept in the prototype.** These are about *integrity*, not security. An LLM asked to "prove the goal" does sometimes take shortcuts, and these checks are what stop the board from lying to you:
1. **Footprint check.** Lean's `#print axioms` must show only your selected assumptions, Lean's 3 standard axioms, plain vocabulary, and the presuppositions (D-5).
2. **No `sorry`** in anything shown as proved.
3. **Statement unchanged.** Claude proves exactly the statement you see in the review, so it cannot quietly weaken the goal. This uses `lake comparator`, which is built into Lean 4.35 and takes about 3 s.
4. **Simple vocabulary rule.** Claude may add only plain types (`axiom T : Type`), predicates (`… → Prop`) and named constants. Any definition or structure is shown to you for a yes/no, because definitions can quietly encode beliefs.
5. **No shell for Claude.** It edits a copy of your model files, and nothing touches your files until you accept the diff.
6. **Lean builds run under a memory cap** (your RAM history) **in a basic sandbox**: no network, home folder hidden. Lean files can execute code while they compile, so this is one small wrapper around the already-installed `bwrap` + `systemd-run`.
7. **Opt-in per folder.** telelean only switches on in folders you initialise.

**Deferred to an optional hardening milestone (H)**, to do if you ever share telelean or want belt-and-braces:
- symlink-proof confinement of Claude's file tools (realpath, `O_NOFOLLOW`);
- the fully audited sandbox profile (mount allowlist, D-Bus/keyring socket isolation);
- the complete vocabulary data-type rule for exotic types (`Subtype`, `Sigma`, `Sort u`);
- kernel replay (`leanchecker`) against environment hacking;
- formal-immutability checks on untouched nodes (G5's second half);
- the full exploit-fixture test suite.

Sections D-3, D-24 and D-26 below describe the *full* design. Each says which parts belong to the prototype.

**Recommendation.** A subject is a module subtree plus a namespace: `Model/<Subject>/{Vocabulary,Main,Inbox}.lean` under `namespace <Subject>`.

- Selections and agent context stay within one subject.
- One subject reuses another only through an explicit import.

| Component | Responsibility |

| WorkspaceIndex (runner) | Watches `Model/**/*.lean` in opt-in roots. Default excludes: `.lake/`, `verbatim_prompt_log/`, `test-fixtures/`, `lean/TeleleanTools/`. Incremental parse per subject |

---

## 7. The board (webview UI)

**Rendering.** No graph library supports three independently scrolling viewports that share edges. That covers React Flow, Cytoscape.js, JointJS, Sigma.js and GoJS (surveyed). So the board is three plain scrollable DOM columns plus one **custom SVG edge overlay**. A vanilla prototype of exactly this was benchmarked at about 17 ms per frame with 2,510 nodes and 2,262 edges, and screenshot-tested in dark, light and high-contrast themes (ran in Chrome).

**Stack.**
- React 19 + zustand + CSS on `--vscode-*` variables, and `@vscode/codicons`.
- `@atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop`, which uses native HTML5 drag and never moves DOM, so cached edge geometry stays valid.
- **Shiki** for Lean code: it bundles vscode-lean4's own grammar and uses the JS engine (no WASM). M1 may start with a plain `<pre>`.

**Layout.**
```
<App>  store · HostBridge · ThemeWatcher · SubjectPicker
├─ <Toolbar>  search/filter · edges Auto|Focus|All · ancestors/consequences · legend
├─ <ProposalBanner>  "4 new · 3 changed · 1 moved"  n/p · Review… · Accept · Feedback · Discard · Raw Lean diff…
├─ <Board>  <EdgeLayer under/> <Column type=A|D|G>×3 <EdgeLayer over/> <EdgeBadges/>  (EdgeEngine, imperative)
│     A column: <VocabularyGroup/> (auto-expands "+3 new" in proposals) · cards
├─ <SelectionTray>  premise chips ⊢ [target slot]  · expanded obligation · [Self-evident?] / [These suffice ▶]
├─ <AgentThread>  progress · question cards (answer in place) · Review view · report card · composer "Ask Claude…"
└─ <PromptBox>  Assumption | Derivation | Goal · text · stance chips · why/where-from field · "Add assumption"
```

**Node card.**
- **Face:**
  - checkbox (select), your sentence (plain), and a "because: …" line, but only with *your* rationale;
  - **blue aura** if formalised, one proof glyph, certificate badges, ⚑ decision chips;
  - one "needs attention" badge.
  - Claude's wording appears *italic* with a marker. A test asserts that agent text never renders in user styling.
- **Expanded (chevron):** Lean code; "Depends on / Used by" buttons (which double as the screen-reader route); footprint including presuppositions; Attempts history; wording history; "Open in editor".
- Vocabulary items are box-shaped. Presuppositions carry one chip per type ("assumes characters exist"). Ghost assumptions are translucent with a "Claude suggests" marker; dashing is reserved for your declared support.

**Gestures** (D-17):
- click selects; chevron or Enter expands;
- drag within a column re-orders;
- dragging across columns reveals **labelled drop zones that state the impact**, and dropping elsewhere cancels;
- drag from a port draws a declared arrow;
- in-board Undo (Ctrl+Z when focused) plus an Undo toast;
- keyboard and context-menu equivalents, contributed as VS Code keybindings scoped to the board.

**EdgeEngine.**
- At most one rAF per change. Geometry is cached by ResizeObserver; only three `scrollTop`s are read per frame.
- Edges with both ends off-screen are culled. An edge with one end hidden becomes a stub plus a "▲ n linked / ▼ n linked" button.
- Focused nodes get full curves. Same-column loops go through the gutter, and joint premises meet at a junction dot.
- About 250 drawn edges per frame, prioritised.
- **Line pattern is reserved for epistemic status**: dashed means declared, solid means verified, and it holds in every mode.
- Diffs use colour plus a +/−/~ glyph plus a halo.

**Review view** (D-19). This is the single end-of-run review, done in place on the cards, with a stepper ("3 of 7"). In **M2** it shows your sentence beside the Lean statement, with the fully explicit toggle and the statement closure; **M3** adds alignment, the deterministic gloss and the back-translation. Each new or changed statement shows (full version):
- your sentence with aligned spans underlined; hovering shows the symbol and its type, and unaligned words are flagged ("not represented: *would*");
- the **deterministic gloss** ("Lean says");
- the independent back-translation;
- a toggle to the fully explicit form and the statement closure.

Proof status is revealed after the statements. Pure signature items are grouped and auto-approved, but revocable.

import Model.Spyro.Vocabulary

namespace Spyro

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: pg-no-dark-past
type: ASSUMPTION

stance: rule

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: cynder-dark-past

natural_name: Cynder is a character who has a dark past

source: common

axiom cynder_dark_past.holds : cynder_dark_past

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: new-spyro-pg
type: ASSUMPTION
natural_name: The new Spyro game is PG
rationale: known from gaming news
source: reported
asserted: 2026-11-01
lean: Spyro.new_spyro_pg
-/
/-- The new Spyro game is PG -/
abbrev new_spyro_pg : Prop := IsPG newSpyro
axiom new_spyro_pg.holds : new_spyro_pg

/-
@@ telelean v1
id: cynder-not-good
type: GOAL
natural_name: Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game
premises: cynder-dark-past, new-spyro-pg, pg-no-dark-past
asserted: 2026-11-01
lean: Spyro.cynder_not_good
-/
/-- Cynder would not be a good addition to the new Spyro game -/
abbrev cynder_not_good : Prop := ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro

end Spyro
namespace Spyro

/-- characters -/
axiom Character : Type
/-- games -/
axiom Game : Type
/-- there is at least one character -/
axiom Character.exists : Nonempty Character
instance : Nonempty Character := Character.exists
/-- there is at least one game -/
axiom Game.exists : Nonempty Game
instance : Nonempty Game := Game.exists
/-- has a dark past -/
axiom HasDarkPast : Character → Prop
/-- is rated PG -/
axiom IsPG : Game → Prop
/-- would be a good addition to -/
axiom GoodAddition : Character → Game → Prop
/-- Cynder -/
noncomputable opaque cynder : Character
/-- the new Spyro game -/
noncomputable opaque newSpyro : Game

end Spyro
import Model
namespace Spyro
-- what a run would add under the NORMATIVE reading of pg-no-dark-past
abbrev pg_no_dark_past : Prop := ∀ (g : Game) (c : Character), IsPG g → HasDarkPast c → ¬ GoodAddition c g
axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds : pg_no_dark_past
theorem cynder_not_good.holds : cynder_not_good :=
  pg_no_dark_past.holds newSpyro cynder new_spyro_pg.holds cynder_dark_past.holds
end Spyro
#print axioms Spyro.cynder_not_good.holds

exit 0

input.summary:
WP5 is built and tested. Typecheck is clean, all 80 unit tests pass, and the final isolated VS Code smoke run passes 30/30 (run 5).

What the extension host now does:
- **Opt-in and commands:** it activates on workspaceContains:**/.telelean/config.json and onWebviewPanel:telelean.board. It contributes Open Board, Initialize Model Here (also on the explorer folder context menu) and Refresh Lean Check, plus 6 settings and 6 colour ids. Every colour id has one dot and explicit hex defaults for all four theme kinds, with no charts.*. Untrusted and virtual workspaces are unsupported.
- **Boards:** one BoardPanel per model root, titled "telelean: <folder>". A serializer restores the root and subject after a reload. The host cannot write the webview's state, so it keeps its own record of each board's title, root and subject in workspaceState, and also uses a {root, subject} state if the webview saves one.
- **Workspaces:** one ModelWorkspace per root, created when its first board opens and kept until the window closes, so undo survives closing the board.
- **EditApplier:** checks each file's current text (open buffer first, then disk) against `before`, applies one WorkspaceEdit with minimal line edits (the installed diff package) plus create/delete, then saves.
- **Watchers:** typing is batched for 200 ms and only re-parses. A save re-parses and requests a refresh. File-system events re-read files, and lakefile/toolchain/manifest changes also refresh. `.lake`, `.telelean/graph.json` and the echoes of telelean's own writes are ignored. Lean refreshes are requested only while that root's board is open (D-28).
- **Protocol dispatch:** messages are validated with core's parseWebviewToHost, mapped to BoardActions, and answered with actionResult and Undo-toast notices. Undo, redo, subject switching, createSubject, history list/preview/revert/prune and initGit (after a modal confirmation) are handled. The board switches to the first remaining subject when its subject disappears. copyText writes the clipboard and says "Copied". openInEditor refuses paths outside the root, including symbolic links that point outside. History previews open VS Code's multi-file diff over a read-only telelean-history: provider.
- **Initialize:** inspect → validated subject name (default derived from the folder name) → planInitialize → EditApplier → modal git offer → open the board.
- **Bundle:** the extension imports only the runner's workspace subpath. The build fails if llm/ enters the bundle, and a unit test builds the bundle and loads it with a vscode stub.
- **Fallback:** a build without model workspaces shows the static sample with a warning.

Testing:
- The M0 sample path is kept as openBoard({ sample }), and the M0 smoke tests were updated to use it. The colour test now expects the 6 ids.
- The smoke tests run in a fully isolated profile. The suite against the real WP1–WP4 workspace marks itself pending while they are stubs; WP2's planAction landed during my work, so it ran and passed in runs 3, 4 and 5.

During testing my smoke script deleted npm's own debug logs in the real ~/.npm/_logs, during runs 1–4. Details are under effects; it is fixed in the script.

minor_decisions.decision: A successful undo or redo posts its notice with undoable: false. Other successes use the outcome's undoable flag, so revert keeps its Undo button.
minor_decisions.rationale: The toast's Undo posts `undo`, which would undo the next older action, not reverse the undo itself.

minor_decisions.decision: A refusal posts actionResult (when there is a requestId) and also a warning notice, or an error notice for code 'internal'. The one exception is needs-confirmation with a requestId, which goes to actionResult only so the webview can ask.
minor_decisions.rationale: Nothing fails silently. If WP6 also shows actionResult errors, change BoardSession.finish.

minor_decisions.decision: theseSuffice with no premises is answered by the host with not-yet ("Self-evident?" arrives in M2) and never reaches planAction.
minor_decisions.rationale: The frozen protocol says empty means not-yet. Passing set-premises with [] could be read as 'clear premises'.

minor_decisions.decision: Restoring a board uses the host's own records in workspaceState (title, root, subject) plus the restored panel's title. A {root, subject} (or {telelean: {...}}) saved by the webview is honoured when present.
minor_decisions.rationale: The host cannot write webview state, and the M1 webview does not save root/subject.

minor_decisions.decision: Initialize's git offer and the initGit message call ws.initGit(), not initGitRepository directly.
minor_decisions.rationale: ws.initGit runs git init and also starts the subjects' history chains, so the workspace's history state stays consistent.

minor_decisions.decision: Initialize on an existing Lake project asks a modal 'Add telelean to the Lake project …?' before writing.
minor_decisions.rationale: It modifies an existing project; an empty folder needs only the subject name.

minor_decisions.decision: Settings take effect after a window reload, and the setting descriptions say so.
minor_decisions.rationale: Model workspaces live until the window closes, so undo survives closing the board, and their options are fixed when they are created.

minor_decisions.decision: 'Open in editor' opens beside the board, as a normal (non-preview) tab.
minor_decisions.rationale: Opening in the same column would hide the board.

minor_decisions.decision: The test hooks (api.testing) exist only in ExtensionMode.Test. In Test mode an unanswered modal counts as 'no', and quick picks and folder pickers are never shown.
minor_decisions.rationale: Nobody can click in xvfb, and the hooks must not exist in normal use.

minor_decisions.decision: If the runner functions are still stubs (NotImplementedError), Open Board shows the static Spyro sample with a warning notice instead of failing. The sample board is titled 'telelean: sample'.
minor_decisions.rationale: Keeps M0 behaviour for the user's installed copy until integration.

minor_decisions.decision: Echoes of telelean's own writes are ignored by the watchers. File-system events are skipped for files open in an editor, whose document events cover them. Typing is debounced 200 ms, file events 300 ms.
minor_decisions.rationale: Avoids redundant re-parses and refreshes. The first event with any other text forgets the echo record, so the user's own changes are never dropped.

minor_decisions.decision: Files that telelean deletes (e.g. undoing an add that created a file) go through VS Code's WorkspaceEdit. With files.enableTrash on (VS Code's default) they go to the OS trash.
minor_decisions.rationale: WorkspaceEdit is what makes the batch atomic, and the trash makes deletions recoverable. The tests' deletions landed in the isolated profile's trash.
Explicit hex values for every theme kind, as the M0 lesson asks.

minor_decisions.decision: telelean.git.path has scope 'machine'; the memory settings are 'machine-overridable'; the refresh and snapshot settings are 'resource' (read per root).
minor_decisions.rationale: An executable path should never come from workspace settings.

minor_decisions.decision: Open Board on a board whose model failed to load creates the board again, i.e. retries.
minor_decisions.rationale: Lets a fixed folder load without a window reload.

minor_decisions.decision: vitest's results cache was moved from node_modules/.vite to out/.vite.
minor_decisions.rationale: Keeps test writes inside WP5's assigned paths.

13	
14	**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. 106	**Building the graph.**
107	1. **Parse.** The markup blocks in the subject's `.lean` files are parsed, preferring open buffers to disk (milliseconds).
108	2. **Bind.** Each block is bound to its declarations: pinned `lean:` names win, otherwise adjacency.
109	3. **Merge Lean facts.** Facts from the semantic layer (§5) are merged, keyed by file hash so stale facts show as stale.
110	4. **Add Lean-only items.** Vocabulary, presupposition and untracked items come from declarations that have no block.
111	5. **Validate**, then compute statuses and edges.
112	6. **Publish.** A versioned patch goes to the board, and `.telelean/graph.json` is rewritten (D-27).
113	
114	**`graph.json` schema** (format `telelean-graph` 1.0):
115	- `format`, `format_version`, `generator`, `semantic {available, lean_version, stale}`
116	- `subjects[]`
117	- `nodes[]`, with LSP-convention ranges (0-based, UTF-16)
118	- `edges[]`, `attempts[]`, `diagnostics[]`, and `files[]` with sha256
119	
120	A JSON Schema ships with it. Additive changes are minor versions; breaking changes are major versions, and the previous major stays available for a while. Research prototyped and validated this schema with an example analysis script ("which assumptions does each goal rest on? which are unused?").

124	## 3. Markup language v1
125	
126	### 3.1 Grammar and rules
127	
128	```
129	block  = "/-" NL marker NL { field NL } [ "---" NL body ] "-/"
130	marker = "@@" ws "telelean" [ ws "v" digits ]       ; optional version; absent = v1 (no warning)
131	field  = key ws? ":" ws? value                       ; key = lcid { "." lcid } ; dotted = extension, preserved
132	value  = json-string | raw-text                      ; typed by the key's schema, never by appearance
133	```
134	
135	- **Not YAML.** Raw text may contain `:`, `#` and quotes. A value starting with `"` is a JSON string.
136	- **Escaping, done by the serializer.** A value containing a comment delimiter, or starting with a quote, is written as a JSON string: `-/` becomes `-\/` and `/-` becomes `\u002f-` (backslash, `u`, `0`, `0`, `2`, `f`, then `-`). In the Markdown body they become `-\/` and `/\-`. A stray `/-` would swallow the rest of the file (ran), so round-trip tests check it.
137	- **Detection.** A plain `/- … -/` comment whose first non-blank line is the marker. `/--` and `/-!` are never used for blocks.
138	- **Binding.**
139	  - By adjacency: the next declaration after the block. Its docstring, attributes and modifiers may sit in between, and a blank line means code-less.
140	  - Once formalised, the binding is **pinned** with fully-qualified names (`lean: Spyro.cynder_not_good`), so inserted declarations cannot rebind a node.
141	- **Lexing.** The lexer respects Lean: comments nest, strings hide markers, `«…»` and raw strings are handled. Research verified 19 lexing cases plus 20 parser tests in a Python reference implementation.
142	- **Rules for `id`.**
143	  - Generated from `natural_name` (transliterated; fallback `n-<6 hex>`), unique per workspace, never changed implicitly.
144	  - Markup is UTF-8, and your sentences may be in any language; back-translations use the sentence's language.
145	  - A block without an `id` (like your S37 sketch) is accepted: telelean derives one, writes it back on the next edit or via a quick fix, and reports info TL112.

77	**Why it matters.** S5 calls assumptions axioms, S7 forbids derivations that need new assumptions, and S28 asserts that a *selected subset* suffices. Lean must be able to say exactly which beliefs each result rests on.
78	
79	**Options.**
80	- **(a) Global `axiom`s.**
81	  - `Lean.collectAxioms` gives each theorem's exact, transitive assumption set (ran). On the corrected walkthrough example (03 §3.3), the goal's proof yields exactly: `Classical.choice`, the signature axioms, the presuppositions `Character.exists`/`Game.exists`, and the three `….holds` assumptions (ran).
82	  - `lake comparator` enforces "only these axioms". It rejects a proof that uses a declared but unselected assumption (ran).
83	  - Risk: an inconsistent belief set makes everything provable (handled in D-6).
84	- **(b) Bundled hypotheses**, `structure World …; theorem t (W : World) : …`, the style of your `smoking.lean`. A model is an instance, as with your `paternalismFree`. Dependency tracking needs custom analysis, and the selection must be enforced through statement shape.
85	- **(c) Section `variable`s.** Ruled out: on 4.35 a hypothesis used only in a proof body is not included (ran).

87	**Recommendation: (a), with (b)'s strengths generated.** For consistency or independence, telelean builds the Ramsey sentence `∃ vocabulary, A₁ ∧ … ∧ Aₙ` (and `… ∧ ¬G`). A witness proved using at most `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` is exactly an instance of the bundle structure, i.e. a model (prototyped). 4	
5	## A1 · D-23(a): Claude is driven through your installed Claude Code CLI (the learnharness pattern), behind an LLM-agnostic interface
6	
7	**What telelean does.** It starts `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json …` in a copy of your model files ("the shadow"). The flags allow:
8	- the file tools (Read/Glob/Grep/Edit/Write) and telelean's own tools, and nothing else: no shell, no web;
9	- none of your Claude Code settings, hooks or CLAUDE.md;
10	- no API-key or cloud-provider environment variables, so you are never billed per token by accident.
11	
12	**Where telelean's tools live.** Tools such as `ask_user`, `check_lean` and `finish` are served over a local **MCP** server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the standard way to give an agent tools, and most agent CLIs support it.
13	
14	**What makes it LLM-agnostic.** Telelean's own logic sees only an `LlmBackend` interface: start, send, events, interrupt, resume. Supporting another LLM means writing one adapter. For an agent CLI that speaks MCP, the adapter is its flags plus parsing its event stream; an API-key provider is a further option. Telelean never handles anyone's login or keys.
15	
16	**Which binary.** By default, the Claude Code that ships with your VS Code Claude extension, found automatically. A setting can override it.
17	
18	**Dropped:** the Claude Agent SDK dependency (proprietary licence, plus its own ~330 MB binary).
19	
20	**Traded away:**
21	- *Then:* in-process hooks and typed events. *Now:* a command hook, plus parsing the CLI's JSON event stream.
22	- *Then:* resilience to CLI updates. *Now:* the event stream is more fragile across updates, so a minimum-version check and a recorded stream in the tests catch breakage.
23	
24	**Your reading of the policy is correct, with two nuances.** This is not legal advice.
25	1. **The CLI pattern doesn't "offer claude.ai login".** Each user signs in to their own, unmodified Claude Code, which is the case Anthropic's legal page explicitly allows.
26	2. **The Consumer Terms' clause on "automated or non-human means" still governs subscription use.** You start every run and it waits on your answers, which keeps it ordinary individual use. If you share telelean, the clean route is to point users at an API key or another provider.

import { expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { TlGraph, WebviewToHostMessage } from '@telelean/core';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

export type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'hc';

/** Screenshots land in packages/webview/test-results/. */
export const shotPath = (name: string) => fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../test-results/${name}`, import.meta.url));

declare global {
  interface Window {
    __TL_HARNESS__?: { graph: TlGraph; vars?: Record<string, string> };
    __tlHarness: { posted: WebviewToHostMessage[]; sendToWebview(message: unknown): void };
    __tlCsp: string[];
  }
}

export interface OpenedBoard {
  /** Console errors, page errors and CSP violations seen so far. */
  problems(): Promise<string[]>;
}

export interface OpenOptions {
  /** Extra CSS variables by full name (harness.js applies them after the theme's). */
  vars?: Record<string, string>;
}

export async function openBoard(page: Page, graph: TlGraph, theme: Theme = 'dark', options: OpenOptions = {}): Promise<OpenedBoard> {
  const errors: string[] = [];
  page.on('console', (message) => {
    if (message.type() === 'error') errors.push(`console: ${message.text()}`);
  });
  page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(`pageerror: ${String(error)}`));
  await page.addInitScript(
    ({ g, vars }: { g: TlGraph; vars: Record<string, string> }) => {
      window.__TL_HARNESS__ = { graph: g, vars };
      window.__tlCsp = [];
      document.addEventListener('securitypolicyviolation', (event) => {
        window.__tlCsp.push(`${event.effectiveDirective} blocked ${event.blockedURI || '(inline)'}`);
      });
    },
    { g: graph, vars: options.vars ?? {} },
  );
  await page.goto(`/harness/index.html?theme=${theme}`);
  await expect(page.locator('[data-node-id]')).toHaveCount(graph.nodes.length);
  await settle(page);
  return {
    problems: async () => [...errors, ...(await page.evaluate(() => window.__tlCsp.map((v) => `csp: ${v}`)))],
  };
}

353	## 7. The board (webview UI)
354	
355	**Rendering.** No graph library supports three independently scrolling viewports that share edges. That covers React Flow, Cytoscape.js, JointJS, Sigma.js and GoJS (surveyed). So the board is three plain scrollable DOM columns plus one **custom SVG edge overlay**. A vanilla prototype of exactly this was benchmarked at about 17 ms per frame with 2,510 nodes and 2,262 edges, and screenshot-tested in dark, light and high-contrast themes (ran in Chrome).
356	
357	**Stack.**
358	- React 19 + zustand + CSS on `--vscode-*` variables, and `@vscode/codicons`.
359	- `@atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop`, which uses native HTML5 drag and never moves DOM, so cached edge geometry stays valid.
360	- **Shiki** for Lean code: it bundles vscode-lean4's own grammar and uses the JS engine (no WASM). M1 may start with a plain `<pre>`.

104	**Why it matters.** Vocabulary can smuggle beliefs. All of the following were accepted by `lake comparator` (ran):
105	- a Type-valued record with a Prop field, whose `Nonempty` instance was proved from the very assumption being hidden;
106	- universe-polymorphic `Character : Sort u` instantiated at `Prop`;
107	- `axiom Character : Prop`, whose inhabitants are then all equal by proof irrelevance;
108	- a constant of type `{g : Game // IsPG g}`, whose existence presupposition *is* the belief.
109	
110	**Recommendation.**
111	- **Computed, not marked up.** Vocabulary needs no new markup type. The board shows it, derived from Lean, in a collapsible **Vocabulary** group at the top of the Assumptions column. The group expands with a "+3 new" count whenever a proposal adds vocabulary, so S32's new nodes stay visible. Glosses come from the docstrings, styled as *Claude's wording* until you rewrite them.
112	- **The data-type rule** (enforced by G3, D-26). *The prototype enforces the simple shape check: new axioms must be `T : Type`, predicates ending in `Prop`, constants, or your assumptions. Anything else goes to you for a yes/no. Rule 2's exotic-type cases arrive with hardening (H).*
113	  1. Sort axioms are 0-ary `axiom T : Type` only: no `Sort u`, no universe parameters, and no `axiom T : Prop` used as a sort.
114	  2. Every predicate's binders, every constant's type, and every field or parameter of an endorsed structure or inductive must be a **data type**. That means those sorts, function types between them, or data-only structures and inductives. No `Subtype`, `Sigma`, `PLift`, Prop fields, or `Prop`-indexed families.
115	  3. Predicates and relations end in `Prop`: `axiom HasDarkPast : Character → Prop`.
116	  4. Any other Prop-valued axiom is a belief, i.e. an ASSUMPTION.
117	- **Constants** are `noncomputable opaque cynder : Character`, which needs a `Nonempty Character` instance.

## Prototype profile (personal use): what the first versions include, and what is deferred

*Added after your mid-turn prompt 5.* telelean is a prototype for your own use, and Claude is a cooperative assistant, not an attacker. Most of the security detail that the review rounds surfaced therefore matters only against a deliberately misbehaving model, or for a tool shared with others. The prototype (M1–M2) keeps only what makes the tool's central claim true, plus safety that costs almost nothing. The central claim is: **"proved" means proved from exactly the assumptions you selected.**

**Kept in the prototype.** These are about *integrity*, not security. An LLM asked to "prove the goal" does sometimes take shortcuts, and these checks are what stop the board from lying to you:
1. **Footprint check.** Lean's `#print axioms` must show only your selected assumptions, Lean's 3 standard axioms, plain vocabulary, and the presuppositions (D-5).
2. **No `sorry`** in anything shown as proved.
3. **Statement unchanged.** Claude proves exactly the statement you see in the review, so it cannot quietly weaken the goal. This uses `lake comparator`, which is built into Lean 4.35 and takes about 3 s.
4. **Simple vocabulary rule.** Claude may add only plain types (`axiom T : Type`), predicates (`… → Prop`) and named constants. Any definition or structure is shown to you for a yes/no, because definitions can quietly encode beliefs.
5. **No shell for Claude.** It edits a copy of your model files, and nothing touches your files until you accept the diff.
6. **Lean builds run under a memory cap** (your RAM history) **in a basic sandbox**: no network, home folder hidden. Lean files can execute code while they compile, so this is one small wrapper around the already-installed `bwrap` + `systemd-run`.
7. **Opt-in per folder.** telelean only switches on in folders you initialise.

**Deferred to an optional hardening milestone (H)**, to do if you ever share telelean or want belt-and-braces:
- symlink-proof confinement of Claude's file tools (realpath, `O_NOFOLLOW`);
- the fully audited sandbox profile (mount allowlist, D-Bus/keyring socket isolation);
- the complete vocabulary data-type rule for exotic types (`Subtype`, `Sigma`, `Sort u`);
- kernel replay (`leanchecker`) against environment hacking;
- formal-immutability checks on untouched nodes (G5's second half);
- the full exploit-fixture test suite.

Sections D-3, D-24 and D-26 below describe the *full* design. Each says which parts belong to the prototype.

---

It exists and is empty. What is it for? My suggestion is to make `mental_model/` the sample model workspace (your Spyro walkthrough as subject `Spyro`), possibly as its own git repository.

### D-33 Snapshots and history
**Default.**
- Before applying a proposal, telelean records a snapshot as a **private git ref** (`refs/telelean/snapshots/<run>`). It never touches your branch, index or hooks.
- The Initialize command offers `git init`.
- A History drawer shows accepted changes, including former goals.

### D-34 Reserved for later
**Default.** These are deferred:
- optional `credence` (never defaulting to 50%);
- defeaters and challenges;
- alternative premise sets per goal;
- short handles (h1, h2);
- a typed query syntax mirroring your sketches (`from [h1, h2] ?- g`, `self_evident ?- g`).

input.summary:
WP6 (webview board UI) is complete. All 21 acceptance tests (AT6.1–6.21) are covered by automated tests, and every test passed in my final `npm test` run: typecheck of both configs, Vite build into packages/extension/dist/webview, 75 unit tests and 38 Playwright tests (13 M0 tests, updated where the plan changed them, plus 25 new M1 tests). No frozen file was changed.

What the board does now (React 19 + zustand):
- **Store.** It handles every host message: graph (older versions dropped, the same version re-applied harmlessly), workspace, history, actionResult and notice. Every mutation carries a request id `r<n>`.
- **Optimistic changes.** Drag, add, reorder and in-place edits apply at once and roll back with an error toast if the host refuses. A newly added card keeps a provisional id until the host's graph contains it; `outcome.nodeId` moves its selection and expansion to the final id. A `needs-confirmation` answer opens the dependents dialog with the host's list.
- **Vocabulary group.** Grouped by kind, presupposition chips ("assumes characters exist"), collapsible with the state kept in the webview state, and each item can be highlighted and scrolled to.
- **Card faces.** Aura; one chip per proof status and M1 flag, never a ✓ for a node Lean has not checked; a "checking…" marker on stale nodes; the "needs attention" badge; the D-13 hint; the "uses:" line.
- **Expanded cards.** Lean code with identifier spans, Copy, Open in editor, problems, footprint and presuppositions, Depends on / Used by, stance and source chips, Make Assumption/Derivation/Goal, Edit, Delete.
- **Other UI.** Inline edits, the delete dialog, reorder, D-11 drop zones with the dependents and rationale dialogs, the A|D|G box with stance/why/source, the tray with presupposition chips and a disabled "Self-evident?", the subject picker, the history dropdown, the Lean badge, problems list and banners, toasts with Undo, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y, the extended legend, and the new arrow styles (conditional, mismatch, lean-ref).

The user's four turn-9 requests:
1. **Drag in the code selects text.** The card's `draggable` attribute is switched off at pointerdown inside the code (risk R5); canDrag is also false, and the code has `draggable="false"` and `user-select: text`. AT6.16 passes. Negative controls: with only one of the two mechanisms active the test still passes (either one is enough in Chrome 155); with both disabled it fails (selection length 0, the card drags instead).
2. **"uses:" line.** Built from `lean.uses`, inline "GoodAddition, cynder, …", with a "▾ N" dropdown showing kind and gloss; picking an entry highlights the item.
3. **Copy button.** Posts `copyText` with exactly `lean.code`.
4. **Identifier hover and click.** Hover shows the gloss or the node's sentence; a click highlights the vocabulary item or reveals the card; Ctrl/Cmd+click does nothing yet.

The CSP stays strict: no style attributes; popovers are positioned through the CSSOM, and every test asserts zero CSP violations and zero console errors.

Test isolation: Playwright gives Chrome HOME/XDG directories inside the run's short temp dir, adds `--disable-crash-reporter --disable-breakpad --no-first-run`, and runs under `ulimit -c 0`. A global home guard proves the real home locations are unchanged; my own before/after listing of ~/.config/google-chrome is identical.
input.how_to_run_tests:
cd /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview && npm test
That runs, in order: typecheck (tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p tsconfig.node.json); vite build into ../extension/dist/webview; vitest run (unit tests, Node only); and `sh -c 'ulimit -c 0; playwright test'`.

The Playwright part uses the installed Chrome (channel "chrome"), one worker, and HOME/XDG_* inside a short /tmp/tl-pw-chrome-* directory that is deleted at teardown. A global home guard fails the run if ~/.config/google-chrome, ~/.cache/google-chrome, ~/.cache/fontconfig, ~/.pki or ~/.local/share/pki change.

Screenshots go to packages/webview/test-results/ (gitignored). Check `free -m` first: MemAvailable should be ≥12 GB.

minor_decisions.decision: The Vocabulary group is collapsed by default. Once toggled, the state is kept per board in the webview state, and highlighting an item opens the group.
minor_decisions.rationale: Opened, the 9-item Spyro vocabulary is about 580 px tall and pushes the Assumptions below the fold of a normal window. D-3 already describes the group as one that expands when needed.

minor_decisions.decision: In the A|D|G box, stance chips appear for Assumptions only and source chips for Assumptions and Derivations, not for Goals. In the expanded card the same rule applies, except that a value already set is always shown so it can be removed.
minor_decisions.rationale: Evidentials (observed/reported/…) describe how a belief is known; a goal is not a belief. The why prompt still follows the kind ("Why do you care?").

minor_decisions.decision: The card face is the drag handle. Presses on buttons, fields, the Lean code and the whole expanded area never drag, and clicks in the expanded area never change the selection.
minor_decisions.rationale: This extends request 1 consistently: the expanded area is for reading, selecting text and pressing buttons, and editing in cards is planned later.

minor_decisions.decision: In-place edits (sentence, reason, stance, source) are applied optimistically too. A refused edit rolls back only its own field.
minor_decisions.rationale: Without this the card shows the old text until the host's graph arrives. A per-field rollback cannot overwrite a later edit that succeeded.

minor_decisions.decision: A card the host has not confirmed yet (an add in flight) cannot be dragged, edited or deleted. It is drawn dashed with a 'saving…' chip and survives unrelated graphs until the host's card replaces it (matched by `outcome.nodeId`, or by type and sentence when the graph comes first).
minor_decisions.rationale: The host has no block for it yet.

minor_decisions.decision: Request ids are `r<n>`. The counter is persisted in the webview state, so ids continue after a webview reload.
minor_decisions.rationale: Otherwise an answer to a request sent before a reload could match a new request.

minor_decisions.decision: Dropdowns and tooltips render in document.body, positioned through the CSSOM. They follow their anchor while scrolling and close once it scrolls out of view, on Escape, or on a press outside. They stop click propagation.
minor_decisions.rationale: A column's scroll box would clip them. React bubbles portal events to the card, which selected it (a bug found by AT6.17). Scroll events arrive a frame late, which closed a just-opened menu.

minor_decisions.decision: The same toast text shows once (at most 4 toasts; info 6 s, warning 10 s, error 15 s). Every refused request shows `outcome.error` as an error toast; a needs-confirmation answer to a kind change opens the dialog instead.
minor_decisions.rationale: The host's notice and the board's refusal toast may say the same thing.

minor_decisions.decision: "Revert to this" is offered for every history entry, including the newest.
minor_decisions.rationale: Reverting to the newest snapshot discards unsnapshotted hand edits; the host snapshots the current state first, so it stays undoable.

minor_decisions.decision: Delete is not optimistic: the card stays until the host's graph removes it. The keep-Lean choice is shown only for formalised cards; code-less cards get 'Delete card' alone.
minor_decisions.rationale: Deleting is the least reversible action, and the brief asked for optimism only on drag, add and reorder.

minor_decisions.decision: Dropping a card on itself is 'no move' (nothing is posted). M0 moved it to the end of its column.
minor_decisions.rationale: Reorder now posts and edits layout.json, so an accidental no-op drag should not write anything.

minor_decisions.decision: During a drag, each candidate column shows a drop-zone panel near its bottom with the impact summary and detail (backticks stripped). The panel lets the pointer through. The header keeps M0's 'Drop to make X'.
minor_decisions.rationale: The column header is too narrow for the impact text. A panel that lets the pointer through does not shift cards under the pointer during the drag.
Line pattern stays reserved for epistemic status (D-13/D-15). Tooltips need pointer events, which are limited to the few marked arrows so wheel and clicks still reach the columns.

The raw `#print axioms` list is in a collapsed details element. The proved-goal and provable-assumption chips are buttons that start Make Derivation; the 'no reason yet' chip opens the reason editor. input.integration_notes:
For WP5 and the integrator:

1. **Webview state.** The board merges `{ subject, vocabCollapsed, requestCounter }` into the panel's webview state and preserves any other keys. WP5's panel serializer can read `state.subject` to reopen the same subject.
2. **Message flow.**
   - On `ready` (lastVersion null after a reload), send `workspace`, then `graph`.
   - Answer every mutating message that has a `requestId` with an `actionResult`; for addNode, `outcome.nodeId` is the host's final id.
   - On a refusal the board shows `outcome.error` as an error toast; a notice with the identical text is deduplicated.
   - `needs-confirmation` for a kindChange rolls the card back and opens the dependents dialog listing `outcome.dependents`.
   - `historyList` (sent on dropdown open, with limit 50, more on demand) expects a `history` reply.
   - `selectSubject` and `createSubject` expect the host to post `workspace` + `graph` for the new subject.
   - A graph of another subject resets selection and expansion and drops pending adds.
3. **Undo keys.** The webview itself handles Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y, posting undo/redo when focus is not in a field or dialog. WP5 must not also bind Ctrl+Z to post undo for the board, or undo would run twice. VS Code's own webview undo (execCommand) is harmless.
4. **Clipboard.** copyText carries exactly `lean.code`. The webview shows 'Copied' on the button; a host notice is shown as a toast too. The harness notice text is 'Copied the Lean code to the clipboard.'
5. **openInEditor targets.** Cards send `lean.codeLoc` (or `loc` for code-less cards), vocabulary items send `item.loc`, and diagnostics send their file and range. The Lean badge posts `refresh`.
6. **Colours.** The board reads `--vscode-telelean-vocabulary` and `--vscode-telelean-highlight` with fallbacks. WP5's manifest already contributes them with per-theme hex defaults, and my theme tests pass against it.
7. **Build output.** dist/webview has the same file names as M0 (webview.js, webview.css, boot.js, assets/codicon.ttf). `npm test` in packages/webview rebuilds it. The user's installed extension will show the M1 board after a reload. With the current host, mutations get no actionResult, so optimistic changes simply stay.
8. **Data the board relies on.**
   - `lean.refs` are code-relative; refs spanning lines or overlapping are ignored.
   - `lean.uses` absent hides the "uses:" line.
   - The attention badge counts diagnostics with `nodeId` and severity error or warning.
   - A `TlEdge` with `conditional` gets the hollow arrowhead, `mismatch` the warning colour, and `lean-ref` the focus-only thin arrow.
9. **Test harness** (packages/webview/test/harness/harness.js):
   - auto-replies ok, with nodeId = clientId for addNode;
   - answers historyList with `__TL_HARNESS__.history` and copyText with a notice;
   - sends `__TL_HARNESS__.workspace` before the graph;
   - `__tlHarness.replies` queues failure outcomes;
   - getState/setState persist in sessionStorage across `page.reload()`.

Used by `packages/runner/test/lean/` (the M0 sandboxed-Lean spike). Base project: `../spyro`.

## `overlays/<stage>/`

Files copied over a fresh shadow of `../spyro` to reproduce a run's stages. Each is a complete
replacement of `Model/Spyro/Main.lean`, so the differences are easy to read with `diff`.

| Stage | What a run would have left | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `formalised` | Phase A done: the normative reading of `pg-no-dark-past` formalised (`abbrev pg_no_dark_past` + `axiom pg_no_dark_past.holds`); the goal has no proof | the frozen snapshot (comparator challenge) |
